now. A long-press could be added to `useCardLift` if the menu is wanted there.
tasks.testStrategy:
Verified in the browser: no element with `aria-label=\"Card actions\"` remains on the board; "
right-click still opens the card menu, and Shift+F10 on a focused card still opens it. npm "
test, build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: Everywhere the app can be is a URL: board, card, view
tasks.description: Asked for: a unique URL for each board, each initiative or card on it, and each view of it. The app now writes the URL as well as reading it, and follows the back button.
tasks.details:
Before this the app read about fifteen query parameters on boot and never wrote one: no shareable link, no back button. Now the URL is the app's own state, in both directions.

**The place** is three facts and one canonical query — `/?board=b-atlas`, `/?board=b-atlas&view=timeline`, `/?board=b-atlas&item=init-signup`, or both at once. `lib/url.ts` is the pure mapping (`viewOf`, `urlQuery`, `placeFromQuery`); `lib/useUrl.ts` is the one owner of the URL, reading on the way in and writing on the way out, with a `popstate` listener for the back button.

**Canonical, not merely faithful**: the query is rebuilt from the state every time and anything unrecognised is dropped, so one place has exactly one URL and two people looking at the same thing hold the same link. The other parameters are *intentions* — read once on arrival and normalised away (`?q=`, `?filters=`, `?collapse=`, `?select=`, `?lens=`, `?boundary=`, `?stress=`, `?edit=`).

**History**: a board and a view are journeys, so each is a step the back button undoes; an open card is the same place with something drawn over it, so it rewrites the step it is on. The alternative — a step per card — leaves a duplicate behind on every dismissal, and back then looks broken once before it works.

**Three decisions worth recording.** `?edit=` is an intention, not a place: edit mode is a mode, and the back button must never be the thing that throws a board design away. `viewOf`'s order matches App's render order, so a state that somehow held two flags still resolves to the view on screen. And a link naming a board or a card that is not here — from another dataset, or to something since deleted — lands on what is there rather than on a blank surface under a URL claiming otherwise.

**Also**: the store gained `setView`, the one name-driven door for all seven views, delegating to the existing tab setters so the rules about which view clears what live in one place; the TopBar's tabs now go through it too, so a tab and a link mean the same thing. `?view=mywork` and `?view=boards` — which the old boot parser did not know — now work. The README's deep-link list, which named boards from two datasets ago, is replaced by the scheme itself.

One bug found by reviewing rather than by probing: an absent `view` was read as "no opinion" when it is written as "the board's own flow", so the back button out of the Timeline left the screen on the Timeline under a URL that no longer mentioned it. The two directions now agree, and that is tested.
tasks.testStrategy: 13 new tests in `lib/url.test.ts`: every view named from its flags, precedence, the canonical query per place, one URL per place and no two places sharing one, the round trip, the legacy `view=metrics`, unknown names, and a hand-written link normalising to the same place. Plus a store test that `setView` and `viewOf` agree for all eight names and that exactly one flag is ever set.\n\nVerified in a fresh browser tab (so history starts clean): a first visit normalises to `?board=b-portfolio`; switching board through the picker writes `?board=b-atlas` and adds a step; opening a card writes `?board=…&item=…` without adding one; dismissing it drops the item with no duplicate; the Timeline tab writes `?board=…&view=timeline`, back returns to the Board view, forward returns to the Timeline; all six views load from a URL; a link naming a board and a card that are gone lands on a real board with no panel; and `?board=b-atlas&item=init-trial&q=trial&edit=1` opens the card, narrows the board, starts editing, and normalises the URL to `?board=b-atlas&item=init-trial`. npm test, build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: Type and Kind are properties in Details, and Kind joins the context menu
tasks.description: Asked for: move initiative kind and card type out of the panel's ⋮ menu into the Details tab, and add Kind to the context menu for initiatives.
tasks.details:
Both controls sat behind the panel's ⋮ menu, which made a property look like an action — you could not read an item's type or kind without opening a menu. They are now cells in the Details property grid, beside Status, Priority, Lead and the rest: **Type** for a card (the card types only, so nothing becomes an initiative), **Kind** for an initiative.

An initiative shows no Type cell and does not need one: the type is what makes it an initiative, it is fixed, and the header already wears the chip. What stays in the ⋮ menu is the note about *why* — a menu is where you would look for the missing control, so the missing affordance still explains itself. A card's ⋮ menu is now purely actions (Duplicate, Archive, Delete); the button's tooltip no longer promises a card type it does not have.

The context menu gained **Kind** for initiatives, next to where a card's Type sits. It is offered only when the *whole* selection is initiatives — the exact mirror of hiding Type whenever any of it is one, so nothing offered applies to "some of the group". The flyout lists None and the board's kinds with the one worn marked, and a kind defined on another board still appears (tagged "another board"), because the menu must not lie about what the item says.

`setItemsKind` is new: the menu acts on a selection, so the setter does too, refusing a kind no board defines for the whole selection rather than half-applying it, and setting it only on the initiatives in a mixed one. `setInitiativeKind` now delegates to it, so the rule lives in one place.

One thing left as it was: on a board that defines no kinds, the Kind control offers only None. It is a real control with nothing to choose (the Kind *filter* hides itself in that case), and it could hide itself the same way — left visible for now, since it is also how a person discovers that kinds exist.
tasks.testStrategy: A store test for `setItemsKind`: a mixed selection sets the kind on its initiatives and nowhere else, clearing is the same gesture, and an id no board defines is refused for the whole selection. Verified in the browser: a card's Details reads Type (User Story|Epic|Bug|Spike|Task) with no Kind, and its context menu has Type and no Kind; an initiative's Details reads Kind with no Type, its ⋮ menu still carries the \"type is fixed\" note, and its context menu has Kind and no Type; on the Growth value stream the Kind flyout reads None | Workstream | Enabler with the worn one checked, and picking Enabler wrote it to the item. npm test, build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: The initiative card leads with its kind, its title and what is under it
tasks.description: Asked for: kinds identifiable at a glance by colour, an initiative shape clearly different from a card, and the focus on the title, the kind and the children's statuses — with the issue codes demoted.
tasks.details:
The wide card was a card with more on it. It is now a different shape.

**The kind is a band across the top**, in the kind's own colour, with the picker behind it. A card is tinted by its type and railed down the left; an initiative wears its kind as a band — so the two are told apart before either is read, and a reader can see what sort of initiative it is without reading a word of the title. `KindChip` became `KindBand`, and it now takes an optional kind and an optional `onSet`, so it can render the empty slot too.

**When the band shows**: whenever the item wears a kind, or the board defines any. A board that defines none shows no band — there is nothing to say and nothing to choose, the same rule the Kind filter keeps. A board that defines some shows the band even on an initiative wearing none, reading "No kind" and offering the board's kinds: the empty slot is how a person discovers that kinds exist, and it is the slot they click to fill. In edit mode the band stays and stops being a control — the previous chip vanished there, which lost the initiative's identity exactly when the board was being designed.

**The reading order is now the priority order**: the band, then the title at `text-title` (15px — the largest text on the board) with priority and the reference beside it, then the children's own stages as 12px pips sorted into the columns' order, with the counts (`N below`, `N open`) and the rollup percentage, then a full-width progress bar, then the warnings, then everything quiet — lineage, tags, links, checklist, size, people. The pips carry a tooltip naming each child and its stage, and the row's own tooltip sums the spread ("7 directly below: 3 done, 2 in progress, 2 not started").

**The reference is demoted**, not removed: `INIT12` is how an initiative is *named* in a standup, not how it is read, so it is 11px, grey, right-aligned and out of the reading path. The size moved to the quiet footer, and the old `Layers N` icon went — the pips say it better.

**One contradiction the redesign exposed and fixed**: the pips were built from the children *excluding* archived ones, while `childCount` and the rollup counted all of them — so an initiative whose only child had been filed away read "nothing below" and "1 below" at once. The pips now cover the same set the rollup does, which is the domain rule the tests already state (`archived leaves still count toward rollup but not toward open pressure`).

Also fixed while in there: the kind picker had no keydown handler, so Escape with its list open bubbled to App and closed the whole panel — the same bug the tag field had.
tasks.testStrategy: No component tests exist (the vitest environment is node), so this is verified in the browser. On the Growth value stream (which defines Workstream and Enabler): the band reads WORKSTREAM in the kind's colour with white text; a new initiative's band reads NO KIND in neutral slate and lists None | Workstream | Enabler when clicked; picking Enabler turns the band slate, retitles it ENABLER and writes `kind-b-portfolio-enabler` to the item; Escape closes the list rather than the board. On Team Atlas (which defines no kinds) there is no band, and the shape still reads as an initiative: 15px title, status pips, full-width bar, quiet footer — beside the cards workflow's small tinted notes with their type chip and left rail. `npm test` (312), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: One badge set for every warning, in one place, and bigger child indicators
tasks.description: Asked for: larger initiative child indicators, and blocked / uncommitted / other warnings as a consistently positioned set of badges.
tasks.details:
**The child indicators are 16px** (were 12), with a 4px radius, still sorted into the columns' order and still capped at twelve with a `+N`.

**The warnings are now one set of badges in one place**: a row between the progress bar and the quiet footer, so a reader scanning a column knows where to look and a card with nothing to say says nothing. The set is `initiativeHealth`'s own flags — the same rules, the same words and the same tones the dashboard's Health column reads, so an initiative cannot be at risk in one place and quiet in another.

**One shape, two weights.** Every badge is the same size, radius and type scale; the tone carries the domain's own distinction. A hard stop is solid (`bg-rose-600`, bold) — the card has always drawn a blockage that way, "so a blockage anywhere beneath it reads at a glance rather than as another piece of metadata" — and something to watch is pale, ringed and lighter in weight, so a card carrying four watches does not shout the way a card carrying a blockage does. The words and the titles are the domain's: a badge never invents its own vocabulary.

**Two exceptions the card owns**, both commented at the site: "nothing below" is not repeated as a badge because the children row already says it where the pips would be; and a blockage rolled up from team cards keeps the softer tone and the "blocked below" wording the card has always given it, so a programme reader is not shouted at with a fact three levels down. "Waiting on" moved out of the footer into the set: it is the one warning the health rules do not own, because it is about the item itself rather than the work below it. The dependents signal joined the set too, in the same shape and tone as the other watches.

**Cost, measured, because health is the one derivation on this surface that is not linear in the size of the board** — the waiting rule walks the links once per open descendant and the staleness rule looks up a placement for each of them. On `?stress=300` (298 cards, nine initiatives) it is worth about 33ms per change to the work. So it is computed once per change to the work rather than once per render, in a `useMemo` keyed on the store's own arrays plus the day (one rule counts days, and a board left open overnight must not go on saying "still 12d"). Measured A/B against the previous commit: a selection on the stress board costs 118.5ms before and 114-122ms after — the memo holds, and the interactive path pays nothing. The residual is a domain-side characteristic the dashboard has always had (O(open × links)); a links-by-endpoint index in `derive` would fix it for both surfaces, and is not done here.
tasks.testStrategy: No component tests exist (the vitest environment is node), so this is verified in the browser. On the Growth value stream: `1 blocked below` renders pale with the softened wording on the board's own flow while `1 blocked` renders solid in the Linked boards band beneath it; `1 waiting` is solid and `still 7d` / `21 pts below` / `2 backlog` / `1 due later` are pale; all of them sit in one row under the bar. On Team Atlas the pips are visibly larger, and the cards workflow's narrow cards are unchanged. `npm test` (312), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: An initiative's drawer opens with its warnings, and the cards they are about
tasks.description: Asked for: clicking an initiative that has warnings should open the drawer with a warnings section listing the issues and taking you to the relevant cards and board.
tasks.details:
The Details tab — which is what the drawer opens on — now leads with a **Warnings** section, for an initiative that has any. Each warning is its badge (the same shape and the same two weights the card's row uses), the rule's own words beside it, and **the cards the rule found** as rows: a type dot, the reference, the title, the board when it is not the one you are looking at, and an arrow. Clicking a row takes you to that board, the board's own view, and that card's drawer — the order matters, because choosing a board clears the selection by design, so the drawer is opened after it. Up to four cards are named, then the rest are counted.

**The rules now name their members.** `HealthFlagInfo` gained `items`, and `blockedBelow` was split into `blockedBelowItems` with the count as its length, so a badge and the cards it points at cannot drift. The flags about the *shape* of the whole (`stale`, `oversized`) and the one about there being none (`unplanned`) name no cards, with a comment saying why: listing the entire work below under "nothing has moved" would be a list of everything, which is not navigation. The `uncommitted` rule now takes its list from `leafItems` rather than its count from `uncommittedBelow` — the same leaves `rollupOf` counted — so the badge can point at them.

The dependents signal joins the set, as it does on the card: it is a fact about this item rather than a health rule, and the card already draws it as one of the same badges.

An **Open on the board** action appears only when there is somewhere to go — a view that is not the board, or an item that lives on another board — so it is never a control that does nothing.

Health is memoized on the store's own arrays plus the day, for the same reason the board memoizes it: it is the one derivation here that is not linear in the size of the initiative, and a drawer that recomputed it on every keystroke in the description field would stutter.

The badge grammar moved to `lib/colors` (`FLAG_BADGE_SHAPE` / `FLAG_BADGE`) so the card's row and the drawer's section are visibly one set rather than two lookalikes. Two grammar bugs the new section made visible were fixed: "1 card below wait on work" and "1 item depend on this".
tasks.testStrategy: Two new domain tests: each flag's `items` is exactly the cards the rule counted and the number in the label is that list's length; and the shape-of-the-whole and nothing-below rules name no cards. In the browser, on Billing migration (six warnings): the drawer opens on Details with the section, each warning carrying its cards; clicking \"Retire the legacy coupon service\" lands on `?board=b-atlas&item=st-coupon-retire` with that card's drawer open and the initiative in its lineage. On the Growth value stream's own Onboarding journey, whose backlog cards live on Team Atlas, the rows name the board and clicking one lands on `?board=b-atlas&item=init-trial`. From the Timeline, the section offers \"Go to Team Atlas with this initiative open\" and it does. `npm test` (314), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: Objectives are reachable, readable, and can be made where they are read
tasks.description: Three reports: the OKR page had no way in but a portfolio board's corner; its dark header was hard to read and did not say what to do; and a portfolio offered no way to add an objective.
tasks.details:
**A way in, in the navigation.** `Objectives` is now a tab beside Archive and My work — it is organisation-level, not any one board's, so it sits with the other organisation-level views. It goes through `setView`, so it is addressable like everything else: clicking it lands on `?board=b-atlas&view=objectives`, which is a link somebody can send. The Boards workspace hides the nav (it always has), so the workspace carries its own block — *Objectives & Key Results · N objectives · M key results — what the work is for, and the strategic initiatives that serve it* — above the board grid.

**A header that can be read.** The page's header was a dark strip: `text-slate-600` on `bg-slate-800`, which is **1.9:1** against this app's own 4.5 floor — the legibility rule it tests for in `lib/legibility.test.ts`. It is now the light, tinted panel the other views use (Archive's amber, Boards' indigo, this one violet): an eyebrow, a heading that says how many objectives this period and whether that is over the commitment limit, and a line saying what the page is for. The primary action is a named button — *New objective* — beside the period it will land in, instead of a bare `Objective` at the far end of a dark bar. A new test pins the pairs (and the old strip, as the reason it went).

**Making one where it is read.** The strategy map now has the same control: name an objective in the header and it is created in the latest period the map already shows, arriving as a card with its coverage gap inline — *No strategic initiative serves this OKR* — and the *Map a strategic initiative* control right there, which is the next thing to fix. The empty state no longer sends you to another page to do it.

The objectives button in the strategy map's section header stays: it goes to the *editing* view (period, key results, scores), which is a different errand from making one.
tasks.testStrategy: A new legibility test: the header's three pairs clear the floor on violet-50, and slate-600 on slate-800 does not — the measurement that made the case. In the browser: the nav's Objectives button lands on `?board=b-atlas&view=objectives`; the workspace block reads its counts and lands on the same place; the header reads 3 of 5 this period with the explanation line legible; naming an objective on the page creates it (3 → 4, and the heading follows); and on Company Strategy, naming one in the map creates it (4 → 5) as a card reading \"No strategic initiative serves this OKR\" with its map control. `npm test` (315), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: A portfolio reads its objectives through its own initiative workflow
tasks.description: Asked for: users connect OKRs to initiatives, and the initiatives appear under that objective in a consistent initiative workflow — the connection and the progress read together.
tasks.details:
The strategy map used to list each objective with its serving initiatives as compact rows: ref, title, kind chip, health chip, percent, stage chip. That said everything and showed nothing — the stage was a chip rather than the column it is everywhere else, and the map was a report *about* the flow rather than the flow.

Now each objective heads **its own initiatives workflow**: this board's own typed columns, the same ones a team board shows, narrowed to the strategic initiatives attributed to it. The initiative sits in the column its own work puts it in, wearing the same card it wears everywhere — kind band, title, children pips, rollup, warnings — so the connection and the progress are read in one place, in the language the rest of the app already speaks.

**The mechanism is one prop.** `BoardSummary` gained `onlyIds`, and everything downstream follows from that single narrowing: a cell's badge counts the group's initiatives, and the health is found for them alone. That last part matters — the health rules are not linear in the size of a board (the waiting rule walks the links once per open descendant), and N groups must not each pay for the whole board. The memo is keyed on the ids as one string, because whoever passes the array rebuilds it every render.

**One objective per row.** The first cut kept the three-across grid and gave every column a twelfth of the page — narrower than the card it had to hold, so titles broke mid-word and the column names truncated. A flow needs the width; the groups stack.

**The gaps stay first-class.** An objective nobody serves says so in words instead of drawing four empty boxes — 'nothing yet' and 'served from somewhere else' are different facts and neither is a workflow. An initiative serving no objective gets a flow of its own at the end, with the instruction that maps it: 'map one from the objective it belongs to', which is the direction the per-objective *Map a strategic initiative…* control already works in.

**The flow here is read-only, deliberately.** An initiative may serve several objectives — attribution is a relation, not a container — so the same card can appear in more than one flow, and a lift/drop would not know which group it was rearranging. Making it draggable means answering that first.

Also fixed, found by clicking around in it: a **read-only kind band swallowed the click** — it stopped propagation before checking whether it was a control, so on a surface that only reads another board's flow, clicking the band did nothing instead of opening the card.

AGENTS.md and the README said the map 'replaces the initiatives workflow'; both now say it *is* the workflow, grouped by what the work is for.
tasks.testStrategy: No component tests exist (the vitest environment is node), so this is verified in the browser. On Company Strategy: each objective heads four typed columns; Recurring revenue engine sits in In Progress (1) with the other columns empty, wearing its kind band, its children pips, 10% and its four warnings; Improve reliability reads '0 serving' with the coverage note and no empty columns; the unmapped initiative has a flow of its own. Mapping INIT3 from an objective's control wrote `obj-activation→init-trust` and moved it into that objective's flow ('1 serving' → '2 serving'). Clicking a card in a group opens the drawer, and so does clicking its read-only kind band. A team board's own flow is unchanged. `npm test` (315), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: A portfolio shows its objectives and nothing else
tasks.description: Asked for: no Linked boards on portfolio boards — just the objectives, their key results, and the initiatives attributed to them in their grouped flows.
tasks.details:
The Linked boards section — and the line under it explaining what a band is — now renders on a **program** board only. A portfolio's surface is its strategy map and nothing else, which is the reading it exists for: what the work is *for*, and the initiatives that serve it, grouped by the objective they answer to.

The links themselves stay in the model, so this is a decision about one surface and not about the data — a programme under a portfolio still rolls up. They are still manageable: **Board settings** has carried the linked-boards list for every aggregating board all along, and a portfolio now says there why its own surface will not show them: "A portfolio shows no bands: these roll up on the programme boards beneath it." Said where the link is made, because that is where somebody would otherwise wonder why nothing happened.

One correctness fix alongside it, in the spirit of the ask: an objective's flow now holds **any** of the board's initiatives attributed to it, not only the local top-level ones. `serving()` read from `mine` — which exists to keep a nested initiative from being a second row the map *heads* — but the OKR page will happily attribute a nested one, and then it belonged in that objective's flow and was missing from it. Coverage still reads `mine`: an outcome is committed or it is not, and a piece of one is not a separate commitment.
tasks.testStrategy: In the browser: on Company Strategy the page reads STRATEGY MAP with three objective groups, no 'Linked boards', no 'roll up here' and no band note; on the Growth value stream the section is still there ('2 boards roll up here'). Board settings on a portfolio still lists its links and carries the new note; on a programme it carries the general note and not the portfolio one. `npm test` (315), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: A board that renders no cards workflow does not make cards
tasks.description: Asked for: remove the + Card button from a portfolio board.
tasks.details:
The toolbar's **Card** button and the palette's **New card** verb are now offered only on a board that renders a cards workflow. Both asked the domain the same question — `isAggregating` — so the two ways in cannot disagree, the same way `isBoardSurface` already answers the toolbar and the side panels.

It is stated as that rule rather than as "not on a portfolio" because a **programme** board has the same property: it shows the initiatives workflow and its linked bands, and no cards workflow either, so a card made there was equally one nobody could see on the board that made it. If a programme board should keep the button, it is one line.

**Initiative stays on both.** It is what a coordination board is read for: on a portfolio the new initiative arrives in the strategy map with its coverage gap, waiting for an objective to carry it — which is the flow the map was built around.

The card still exists as a model fact on such a board (the store will take one, and it reads in My work, the Archive and the Flow metrics) — this is the UI declining to offer something it cannot show, not the model refusing it.
tasks.testStrategy: In the browser, per band: a **portfolio** offers `Initiative` alone in the toolbar and `New initiative` alone in the palette; a **programme** the same; a **team** board offers both, in both places. `npm test` (315), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: An initiative serves one objective
tasks.description: Reported: the same strategic initiative could be mapped to several OKRs. Restricted to one.
tasks.details:
Attribution was a relation — many initiatives to many objectives — and the app made a feature of it ("Serves 2 OKRs — still 1 unit of WIP"). It is now **one objective per initiative**, and the shape is the one the rest of the model already uses for a single choice: **choosing again moves it**, the way `setParent` moves a card and a kind replaces a kind. Nothing accumulates, nothing is refused — the choice replaces the choice.

`setAttribution` is the one door and keeps the rule: mapping to an objective the initiative already serves changes nothing (rather than adding a second edge), mapping to a new one drops whatever it served before, and unmapping leaves it serving none.

**Persistence version 31**, with a migration: state from before the rule keeps the first objective each initiative was mapped to and drops the rest. The same reasoning as v12, which dropped attributions pointing at non-initiatives — an edge the model would refuse is not an edge. Without the bump the normalisation would never run, because zustand only calls `migrate` when the stored version differs.

**The panel's control became a choice.** It was a list of checkboxes under "Map an OKR" — a multi-select, which is what the model no longer is, so the control would have been lying about it. It is now the select the kind and the type use, reading "No OKR" or the objective it serves, with that objective's key results under it. The "Serves N OKRs" line is gone with the rule it described.

**Both mapping selects say when a choice will move something**: an initiative that already serves another objective is offered as "… — moves from <objective>", so the move is visible before it happens rather than discovered afterwards.

The README's "What to try" bullet made the old rule its example ("serves 2 objectives; WIP stays 1") and now says what happens instead.
tasks.testStrategy: Two new tests. Store: mapping to a second objective moves it (one edge, the first gone), choosing what it already serves changes nothing, and clearing leaves none. Migration: state carrying two attributions for one initiative keeps the first and drops the second, while other edges are untouched. In the browser: the map's select offers \"INIT1 Recurring revenue engine — moves from Grow activation\"; mapping it left Grow activation at 0 serving with its coverage note and the gap count at 3, and put it in Reduce cost to serve at 2 serving, in its column; the drawer's control is a select reading \"Reduce cost to serve · FY26 Q4\", and choosing Grow activation moved it back, one attribution per initiative throughout. `npm test` (317), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: A header is drawn only when there is something to put in it
tasks.description: Reported: an initiative with kind None showed a band saying "No kind". It now shows no band at all.
tasks.details:
The initiative card's kind band rendered whenever the item wore a kind **or the board defined any** — the second half was mine, from task 89, on the argument that the empty slot is how a person discovers kinds exist and is the slot they click to fill. That argument loses to the better one: a header for an absence is a header for nothing. It is also what the card did before the redesign ("Unset means absent, so nothing renders without one") and what the app says everywhere else about a label nobody set.

So the band is drawn only when there is a kind to draw, and `KindBand` takes a required kind instead of an optional one. Everything the empty slot was doing for discovery is done elsewhere and better: the board's **Kind filter** sits in the initiatives-flow heading whenever the board defines kinds, and setting one has two homes — the drawer's Kind field and the card menu's Kind.

**What was not changed, and why**: a *card* always has a type — `typeId` is required in the model, so there is no such thing as a card with no type, and its chip is never a header for nothing. The one adjacent case is a type id the workspace does not define, which renders the label "Item" — on the board, the dashboard, the timeline, the archive and in the drawer alike. Making only the card render nothing there would put the board out of step with every other surface, so it is left consistent and flagged rather than changed.
tasks.testStrategy: In the browser on the Growth value stream (which defines kinds): an initiative with no kind — Onboarding journey, with its kind cleared from the drawer's Kind field — renders **no band at all**, while Reliability programme and Enterprise SSO keep their WORKSTREAM bands in the same column. The card menu still offers Kind, and the drawer still shows it as a field, so the label remains settable from both. `npm test` (317), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: The cumulative flow diagram stacks the way the board reads
tasks.description: Asked for: reverse the CFD's columns so Backlog is at the top and Done at the bottom.
tasks.details:
The bands were stacked `flex-col-reverse` over the canonical stage order, which put Done at the top and Backlog at the bottom — the usual CFD convention, where the delivered band grows upward. They now stack in the order the board reads: **Backlog at the top, then Not Started, In Progress, Done at the bottom**, so a column on the board and a band in the chart are the same way round.

A side effect worth having: the legend under the chart already listed the stages in that order, so it now reads top-to-bottom with the bands instead of against them.

One word of CSS (`flex-col-reverse` → `flex-col`) and a comment saying why, since the previous order was the convention rather than an accident.
tasks.testStrategy: In the browser on Team Atlas's Flow view, reading the bands' bounding boxes down the last column: Backlog: 3, Not Started: 2, In Progress: 5, Done: 2 — top to bottom in that order, matching the legend. `npm test` (317), build, lint and the dependency scan are clean.

tasks.title: An initiative has no estimate, and its progress counts all the work below it.
tasks.description: This task changes the progress formula for an initiative. The task removes the estimate property from an initiative. The size of an initiative is the sum of the sizes of the items below it.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The rollup calculation in src/domain/derive.ts.
2. The estimate field on an initiative, in the store and in the user interface.

DEFINITIONS
- Item: a card or an initiative.
- Leaf: an item with no children. `leafItems` returns the item itself if the item has no children.
- Estimate: the `size` field of an item. The unit is points.
- Rollup: the result of `rollupOf`. The result contains `percent`, `size`, `bucket` and counts.
- Bucket: the stage of an item, derived from the leaves below the item. The values are `backlog`, `notStarted`, `inProgress` and `done`.
- Stage of a leaf: the stage of the typed column that holds the leaf.
- Completed leaf: a leaf that is not in the Backlog stage and that `statusOf` reports as resolved.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Progress denominator
The application shall calculate `Rollup.percent` as the total size of the completed leaves below an item, divided by the total size of all the leaves below the item, multiplied by 100.

R2 — Unsized leaf
The application shall count 1 point for each leaf that has no estimate.

R3 — Range
The application shall return `Rollup.percent` as a whole number in the range 0 to 100.

R4 — Estimate on a card
The application shall let a user set an estimate on a card.

R5 — Estimate on an initiative
The application shall not let a user set an estimate on an initiative.

R6 — Estimate control
The application shall not show an estimate control for an initiative in the drawer.

R7 — Estimate control in the card menu
The application shall not show the Size control for an initiative in the card menu.

R8 — Size read-out
The application shall not show the points read-out on an initiative card.

R9 — Oversized rule
The application shall remove the `oversized` rule from `initiativeHealth`.

R10 — Persisted state
When the application loads persisted state that contains an estimate on an initiative, the application shall remove the estimate.

R11 — Persist version
When a persisted shape changes, the application shall increase `PERSIST_VERSION` and shall normalise the shape in `migrateState`.

R12 — Existing tests
The application shall update each test that asserts the previous denominator. The updated test shall assert the denominator in R1.

CONSTRAINTS
- The calculation of `Rollup.size` shall not change.
- The calculation of `Rollup.bucket` shall not change.
- The calculation of the `uncommitted` count shall not change.
- The `outlasted` rule in `initiativeHealth` shall not change.
- The estimate on a card shall not change.

RATIONALE
The progress of an initiative is the size of the completed work below the initiative, divided by the size of all the work below the initiative. The previous formula divided by the committed work only. Unplanned work did not count. After this change, the percentage of an initiative decreases when a user adds an unplanned card below the initiative. This result is correct. The number shows the work.
An initiative is a roll-up. An initiative is not a work item. An estimate on an initiative duplicates the estimates of the children. Two sources for one number can disagree. The application removes one source.
The `oversized` rule compares the work below an initiative with the estimate of the initiative. An initiative has no estimate after this change. Therefore the rule has no input. The application removes the rule.

OUT OF SCOPE
- The estimate of a card.
- The `outlasted` rule.
- Forecasting and delay calculations.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: In a domain test, build an initiative with three leaves. Sizes: 1, 1, 1. Stages: Done, In Progress, Backlog. Assert `Rollup.percent` is 33.
V2 — R1: Build an initiative with two leaves. Sizes: 8 in Done, 2 in Backlog. Assert `Rollup.percent` is 80.
V3 — R2: Build an initiative with one leaf that has no estimate. Assert the denominator is 1.
V4 — R3: Assert `Rollup.percent` is a whole number in the range 0 to 100 for each of the two cases above.
V5 — R12: Run the domain tests. Assert no test asserts the committed denominator.
V6 — R4, R5: In a store test, set an estimate on a card. Assert the estimate is present. Set an estimate on an initiative. Assert the estimate is absent.
V7 — R6: In the browser, open an initiative. Assert the drawer has no Estimate field. Open a card. Assert the drawer has an Estimate field.
V8 — R7: In the browser, open the card menu of an initiative. Assert the menu has no Size control. Open the card menu of a card. Assert the menu has a Size control.
V9 — R8: In the browser, assert an initiative card shows no points read-out.
V10 — R9: In a health test, assert the `oversized` flag does not occur. Assert the `outlasted` flag occurs for an initiative with a child that is due later.
V11 — R10, R11: In a migration test, supply persisted state with an estimate on an initiative. Assert the estimate is absent after the migration.

tasks.title: An OKR has no progress on a key result. The completeness of an OKR comes from the initiatives that serve it.
tasks.description: This task removes the measurement fields from a key result. The task adds a roll-up calculation for an objective. The calculation uses the work below the initiatives that are attributed to the objective.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The `KeyResult` type and the store actions that add, update and remove a key result.
2. The Objectives view, the strategy map and the drawer.

DEFINITIONS
- Objective: an entity with a title, a period, a status and a score. An objective is not a card.
- Key result: a statement that belongs to an objective.
- Strategic initiative: an initiative that a portfolio board carries. `isStrategicInitiative` decides this condition.
- Attribution: an edge of kind `attribution` from an objective to an initiative.
- Objective rollup: the rollup of the union of the leaves below all the initiatives that are attributed to an objective.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Key result fields
The application shall store a key result with the fields `id`, `objectiveId` and `title` only.

R2 — Measurement fields
The application shall not store the fields `progress`, `target` or `current` on a key result.

R3 — Objective rollup
The application shall calculate the completeness of an objective as the total size of the completed leaves below the attributed initiatives, divided by the total size of all the leaves below the attributed initiatives, multiplied by 100.

R4 — Shape
The application shall return the same `Rollup` shape for an objective as for an item.

R5 — Objective with no initiative
If an objective has no attributed initiative, then the application shall return no rollup for the objective.

R6 — Several initiatives
When two or more initiatives are attributed to one objective, the application shall count each leaf below those initiatives one time. The application shall not average the percentages of the initiatives.

R7 — Objectives view
The application shall show the objective rollup for each objective in the Objectives view.

R8 — Key results in the Objectives view
The application shall show the key results in the Objectives view as a list of titles. The application shall not show a progress control for a key result.

R9 — Strategy map
The application shall show the objective rollup in the header of each objective group in the strategy map.

R10 — Drawer
The application shall show the objective rollup in the Strategic impact section of an initiative.

R11 — Key result controls
The application shall let a user add a key result, rename a key result and remove a key result.

R12 — Persisted state
When the application loads persisted state that contains `progress`, `target` or `current` on a key result, the application shall remove those fields and shall keep the title.

CONSTRAINTS
- The two coverage gaps of `okrCoverage` shall not change.
- The `score` field of an objective shall not change.
- The attribution rule shall not change. An initiative serves one objective at most.

RATIONALE
A user enters the progress of a key result by hand. The application cannot connect that number to the work. The number can disagree with the work. No test can find the disagreement. The application removes the number.
An objective is a grouping mechanism. The work that serves an objective is the set of initiatives that are attributed to the objective. The application calculates the completeness of an objective from that work.
An objective with no attributed initiative has no work. A value of 0% would be incorrect. The application returns no value. The coverage gap shows the condition.
The `score` is the grade of an objective at the end of a period. A person sets the grade. The grade is not a progress value. The application keeps the score.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Objective rollups in the CSV exports. The exports contain no key result data.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1, R2: In a domain test, add a key result. Assert the key result has the fields `id`, `objectiveId` and `title`. Assert the key result has no other field.
V2 — R3, R4: Attribute one initiative to an objective. Assert the objective rollup equals the rollup of that initiative.
V3 — R6: Attribute two initiatives to one objective. The leaves are one completed leaf with size 2 and one Backlog leaf with size 13. Assert the percent is 13.
V4 — R5: Assert an objective with no attribution returns no rollup.
V5 — R3: Assert the coverage gaps of `okrCoverage` are the same as before the change.
V6 — R11: In a store test, add a key result, rename the key result and remove the key result. Assert each operation succeeds.
V7 — R12: In a migration test, supply persisted state with `progress`, `target` and `current` on a key result. Assert the fields are absent and the title is present.
V8 — R7, R8: In the browser, open the Objectives view. Assert each objective shows a percentage. Assert the key results are a list of titles with no percentage input and no checkbox.
V9 — R9: In the browser, open a portfolio board. Assert the header of each objective group shows the same percentage as the Objectives view.
V10 — R10: In the browser, open the drawer of an attributed initiative. Assert the Strategic impact section shows the same percentage.
V11 — R5: In the browser, open the drawer of an objective with no attributed initiative. Assert the coverage note is present and no percentage is present.

tasks.title: A child pip on an initiative card opens that child.
tasks.description: This task makes the status pips on an initiative card operate as controls. A user activates a pip to open the child item that the pip shows.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
The status pips in the wide branch of `components/Card.tsx`.

DEFINITIONS
- Pip: a small square on an initiative card. One pip shows one direct child of the initiative. The colour of a pip is the stage of the child.
- Activation: a mouse click or a tap.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Operation
When a user activates a pip, the application shall open the child item of that pip in the drawer.

R2 — Event isolation
When a user activates a pip, the application shall not open the initiative card.

R3 — Accessible name
The application shall give each pip an accessible name that contains the title of the child and the stage of the child.

R4 — Hit area on a coarse pointer
Where the pointer is coarse, the application shall expand the hit area of a pip.

R5 — Read-only surfaces
The application shall operate the pips on each surface that shows an initiative card. A read-only surface is included.

CONSTRAINTS
- The tab order of a board shall not change. A pip shall not become a tab stop.
- The tooltip of a pip shall not change.
- The number of pips and the order of the pips shall not change.
- The style of a pip shall not change where the pointer is fine.

RATIONALE
A pip already identifies a child. The tooltip of a pip contains the title of the child. The application uses that identity for navigation. This change adds no data.
A pip is a shortcut for a pointer. A board carries one pip for every child of every initiative on it, so making each one a tab stop would put hundreds of stops between the top of a board and the cards below it. The keyboard path to a child is the card's own panel, which already lists them; the pip does not need to repeat it. The pip therefore keeps the semantics and the accessible name of a control without taking a place in the tab order.

OUT OF SCOPE
- The parent chip and the lineage chip of a card.
- Navigation from the warnings section of the drawer. That section already opens a child.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: In the browser, open a team board. Click a pip on an initiative card. Assert the drawer opens on the child item.
V2 — R2: Assert the drawer does not open on the initiative.
V3 — The tab-order constraint: on a board, assert the number of tab stops is the same as before the change, and that no pip takes the keyboard focus.
V4 — R3: Assert the accessible name of a pip contains the title of the child and the stage of the child.
V5 — R5: Open a portfolio board. Click a pip in an objective group. Assert the drawer opens on the child item.
V6 — R4: Set the pointer to coarse. Assert the hit area of a pip is larger than 16 by 16 pixels.

tasks.title: A card dropped on an initiative card becomes a child of that initiative.
tasks.description: This task adds a drop target to an initiative card. A user drags a card onto an initiative card to set the parent of the card.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The card lift in `lib/useCardLift.ts`.
2. The drop resolution in `components/BoardCanvas.tsx` and `components/BoardSummary.tsx`.
3. The `setParent` action in the store.

DEFINITIONS
- Lift: the gesture that picks a card up. The card is in the air between the pointer down and the pointer up.
- Drop target: the element below the pointer that accepts the card.
- Parent: the initiative above an item in the decomposition. An item has one parent at most.
- Cycle: a state in which an item is an ancestor of the item itself.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Parent assignment
When a user drops a card on an initiative card, the application shall set the parent of the dropped card to that initiative.

R2 — Replacement
When the dropped card has a parent, the application shall replace the parent.

R3 — Placement
When a user drops a card on an initiative card, the application shall not change the lane or the cell of the card.

R4 — Target type
If the drop target is not an initiative, then the application shall not set a parent.

R5 — Cycle prevention
If the assignment would make the dropped card an ancestor of the initiative, then the application shall not set a parent.

R6 — Self-parent
If the dropped card is the initiative, then the application shall not set a parent.

R7 — Drop preview
While a card is in the air over an initiative that can accept the card, the application shall mark that initiative as the drop target.

R8 — Refused preview
If the store would refuse the assignment, then the application shall not mark the initiative as the drop target.

R9 — Log entry
When the application changes the parent of an item, the application shall add an entry to the log of the item.

R10 — Target resolution
The application shall resolve the card below the pointer from the rectangles of the rendered cards. The application shall not use `document.elementFromPoint` for a card target.

CONSTRAINTS
- The existing drop targets (lanes and cells) shall not change.
- A drop on empty space shall not change the hierarchy.
- The lift shall move a card between lanes and cells after this change.
- The drawer parent control shall not change.

RATIONALE
A user who wants to set a parent opens the card, opens the menu, and finds the initiative in a list. The initiative is usually on the board. A drag is a shorter operation.
`setParent` replaces the parent. It does not refuse a second parent. This is the model rule: an item has one parent at most.
`setParent` refuses a parent that is not an initiative. The comment in the store states that a cycle cannot occur. The argument is that a parent is an initiative, and the type cannot increase down the tree. That argument depends on the drawer picker, which excludes the descendants of an item. A card target does not exclude the descendants. Therefore the store requires a cycle guard.
Cards are `pointer-events-none` while a card is in the air. This rule lets the lane below the card answer the pointer. Therefore `document.elementFromPoint` cannot find a card. The application resolves the card from the rectangle of the card.

OUT OF SCOPE
- A drop target on a card in the cards workflow.
- Multi-select drag. See task 103.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: In a store test, call `setParent` for a card and an initiative. Assert the edge exists.
V2 — R2: Call `setParent` for an item that has a parent. Assert the item has one parent.
V3 — R4: Call `setParent` with a card as the parent. Assert no edge is added.
V4 — R5: Make item A the parent of item B. Call `setParent` for A with B as the parent. Assert no edge is added. Assert no cycle exists in the graph.
V5 — R6: Call `setParent` for item A with A as the parent. Assert no edge is added.
V6 — R9: Assert the log of the item contains one entry for the change.
V7 — R1, R3: In the browser, open a team board. Drag a card from the cards workflow onto an initiative card. Assert the parent chip appears on the card. Assert the card is in the same lane.
V8 — R2: Drop the card on a second initiative. Assert the parent chip shows the second initiative.
V9 — R7: While the card is in the air, assert the initiative is marked.
V10 — R8: Move the card over an initiative that would cause a cycle. Assert the initiative is not marked.
V11 — The constraints: Drag a card to a different lane. Assert the card moves.

tasks.title: A user can set the parent of several items in one operation.
tasks.description: This task adds a parent control to the bulk bar. A user selects several items and sets one initiative as the parent of all of them.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The bulk bar in `components/BulkActions.tsx`.
2. The store action `setParents`.

DEFINITIONS
- Selection: the set of items that the user selected. The bulk bar acts on the selection.
- Parent: the initiative above an item in the decomposition. An item has one parent at most.
- Candidate: an initiative that the operation accepts as a parent for the whole selection.
- Cycle: a state in which an item is an ancestor of the item itself.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Control
The application shall provide a control in the bulk bar that sets the parent of the selected items.

R2 — Candidate list
The application shall list the same candidates as the parent control in the drawer.

R3 — Single operation
When a user confirms the control, the application shall set the parent of each selected item in one operation.

R4 — Replacement
When a selected item has a parent, the application shall replace the parent.

R5 — Initiative in the selection
When an initiative is in the selection, the application shall set the parent of that initiative.

R6 — Cycle prevention
If the operation would make a selected item an ancestor of the parent, then the application shall not set any parent.

R7 — Atomicity
If the application refuses the operation, then the application shall not change any item.

R8 — Reason
If the application refuses the operation, then the application shall show the reason to the user.

R9 — Log entry
When the application changes the parent of an item, the application shall add an entry to the log of that item.

R10 — Candidate exclusion
The application shall not list an initiative that the operation would refuse for the current selection.

CONSTRAINTS
- The single-item parent control in the drawer shall not change.
- The card menu shall not change.
- The bulk bar shall continue to act on the whole selection.

RATIONALE
A user who breaks down an initiative usually links several cards. The application has a selection and a bulk bar. The bulk bar is the correct place for an operation on a group.
The cycle rule applies to the selection as a group. A user can set item A as the parent of item B. A user can set item B as the parent of item A. A user cannot do both in one operation.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Drag operations. See task 102.
- A parent control on the cards workflow.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1, R3: In a store test, call `setParents` for three cards and one initiative. Assert each card has the parent.
V2 — R4: Call `setParents` for items that have parents. Assert each item has one parent.
V3 — R5: Include an initiative in the selection. Assert the parent of the initiative is set.
V4 — R6, R7: Select two items where the operation would create a cycle. Assert no item changes.
V5 — R9: Assert the log of each item contains one entry for the change.
V6 — R2, R10: In a browser test, select three cards. Assert the control lists an initiative that can accept the selection. Assert the control does not list an initiative that would create a cycle.
V7 — R3: Use the control. Assert each selected card shows the parent chip.
V8 — R8: Force a refusal. Assert the user sees the reason.

tasks.title: The app has one permanent origin, chosen before the first real user.
tasks.description: This task fixes the address the product will live at. Browser storage belongs to the origin, so the choice is made once, before anyone has a workspace to lose.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The deploy target (README, `Deploy target`).
2. `AGENTS.md` (the persisted-state section).
3. The host's domain settings.

DEFINITIONS
- Origin: scheme + host + port. `https://flowline.example` and `https://app.flowline.example` are different origins and do not share storage.
- Workspace: the slice persisted under `flowline-state-v3`.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — One origin
The team shall choose the final production origin and record it in the README.

R2 — No second origin
The product shall be announced at that origin only. Preview hosts are not presented as the product.

R3 — Migration path
Where an earlier origin holds workspaces, the team shall publish export/import guidance before announcing the new one.

R4 — The rule is written down
`AGENTS.md` shall state that moving the app to a new origin abandons the `localStorage` of the old one.

R5 — Previews are recognisable
A preview deployment shall be distinguishable from production without opening the app.

R6 — Testers on a temporary origin
Testers may be set up on a temporary `*.workers.dev` origin before the final domain exists. Their
workspaces on that origin are expected to be stranded when the real domain is attached, and the
workspace export is the bridge that carries one across.

PAUSED — 2026-10-20
The app runs for testers at https://flowline.flowline-team.workers.dev, and that is deliberate:
R6 already records that a temporary origin may be used before the real domain exists. The decision
this task asks for — the permanent origin, and the nameserver move that a Worker custom domain
needs — waits until a domain is registered. Nothing else is blocked by it; the deploy, the headers
and the URL contract all work on the temporary origin.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: The README names the origin; the link resolves to the deployed app.
V2 — R2: The production host and the preview host are different, and only production is linked from the README.
V3 — R4: The rule is present in `AGENTS.md`.
V4 — R5: A pull-request preview URL is distinguishable by hostname.
V5 — R6: The export/import path is written down for testers, and one test workspace actually crosses from the temporary origin to the final one.
tasks.complexityReasoning: A decision plus two documents and a host setting. The weight is that it is irreversible once users exist: the origin owns their storage.

tasks.title: Every push is typechecked, linted, tested and built.
tasks.description: This task adds continuous integration running the repository's own checks, so a green local run means something.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A new workflow in `.github/workflows/`.
2. The `package.json` scripts (`typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build`).
3. The no-Firebase/tracking scan in `AGENTS.md`.

DEFINITIONS
- Green: every step of the workflow succeeds.
- Required check: a branch-protection check that blocks merging to `main`.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Trigger
The workflow shall run on every push to `main` and on every pull request.

R2 — Checks
The workflow shall run typecheck, lint, tests, the production build, and the scan from `AGENTS.md`.

R3 — Failures are visible
A failing step shall fail the workflow, and the step shall be named in the summary.

R4 — Cache
Node modules and the build cache shall be cached against the lockfile.

R5 — Informative, not a gate
The check shall not require a pull request: a direct push to `main` stays allowed, and the run's
result is visible on the commit.

R6 — Pinned
The Node version shall be pinned in the workflow and recorded in the README.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Push a branch; the workflow runs.
V2 — R3: Break a test on a branch; the workflow fails at the test step and names it.
V3 — R2: The workflow file contains the five steps.
V4 — R5: A direct push to `main` is accepted, and the run's result appears on the commit.
V5 — R6: The Node version in the workflow matches the README.
tasks.complexityReasoning: One workflow file plus branch protection. No application code.

tasks.title: The production build is served from a host, with a preview for every pull request.
tasks.description: This task puts the static build behind a CDN host and gives each pull request its own URL.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. Host configuration (Cloudflare Pages or Vercel — one, recorded in the README).
2. `npm run build` producing `dist/`.
3. The URL contract in `src/lib/url.ts`.

DEFINITIONS
- Preview: a deployment of one branch at its own URL.
- Place: a URL the app reads. A place is a query string, never a path.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Production
A push to `main` shall deploy `dist/` to the production origin.

R2 — Previews
A pull request shall upload a version to its own URL, recorded in the run log. (Commenting the URL
on the pull request is deliberately not built: this project does not use pull requests, so the
comment would never fire. Add it if that changes.)

R3 — Deep links
The app shall open correctly at a cold load of any place (`/?board=…&item=…`), with no server rewrite rule required.

R4 — Caching
Hashed assets shall be cacheable indefinitely; the document shall be revalidated.

R5 — Headers
The document response shall carry a content-security policy and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

R6 — Rollback
A previous deployment shall be restorable in one action.

CLOSED — 2026-10-20
Verified: production deploys on a push to main; deep links resolve; hashed assets are immutable and
the document revalidates; the CSP, nosniff and noindex headers are served; and a previous deployment
was rolled back in one action and confirmed live (the bundle named no later release than the one
rolled back to). Previews are unexercised because no pull request has been opened.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Load production; the build hash matches `main`.
V2 — R3: Open a deep link in a private window; the board and the open card are correct.
V3 — R4: `curl -I` an asset and the document; the cache headers differ.
V4 — R5: `curl -I` the document; the two headers are present.
V5 — R6: Roll back to the previous deployment; the app loads.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Host configuration: caching, headers and rollback. The content-security policy for a Vite SPA is the only fiddly part.

tasks.title: A failure in the field is reported with a readable stack, and without personal data.
tasks.description: This task connects the existing error boundary and global handlers to an error service, with source maps and release tags.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` and `src/main.tsx`.
2. A reporting service (Sentry, or self-hosted GlitchTip).
3. The build pipeline (source-map upload).

DEFINITIONS
- Event: one reported error.
- Release: the identifier of the build the event came from.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Capture
Uncaught errors and unhandled promise rejections shall be reported, together with the boundary's caught errors.

R2 — Readable
Source maps shall be uploaded per release, so a stack names the original files.

R3 — Release tag
Every event shall carry the release identifier.

R4 — No personal data
The report shall not contain item titles, descriptions, names, board names or workspace content.

R5 — Optional in development
The app shall run with no reporting configured, and shall not fail when the service is unreachable.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-20
Cloudflare-native: `POST /api/errors` on the app's own Worker, stored in D1 (`flowline-errors`),
read in the Cloudflare dashboard until the app has accounts. The endpoint validates and caps every
field, drops a place's query, stores only a salted hash of the address, and refuses more than 30
reports an hour from one. Verified end to end: a thrown error in the built app reached D1 with its
path and view and nothing else.

R2 IS ONLY PARTLY MET. Buffers carry the message and a stack with function names preserved
(`keepNames`, set on `build.rolldownOptions.output` — Vite 8 minifies with oxc, so an `esbuild`
option is silently ignored), so a report says `at dropCardAt (index-abc.js:1:4821)` — searchable, but not
a line. Resolving to original lines needs source maps plus a symbolication step; that is a
follow-up if the frames prove limiting, and Sentry (whose Vite plugin does exactly that) is the
cheap route to it.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Throw from a control in a preview build; the event appears.
V2 — R2: The stack names `src/components/…` rather than the minified bundle.
V3 — R4: Inspect the payload; no workspace content is present.
V4 — R5: Run the dev server with no service configured; the app works and the error is logged locally.
tasks.complexityReasoning: SDK wiring, source maps and payload scrubbing; the no-personal-data rule is the part that needs care.

tasks.title: The team can see which parts of the app are used, without tracking anyone.
tasks.description: This task adds cookieless, aggregate measurement of views and the handful of actions that matter.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A cookieless analytics script (Plausible, or self-hosted Umami).
2. The view switch and the drawer.

DEFINITIONS
- Event: a named action carrying no identifier.
- Cookieless: nothing is stored in the browser and no fingerprint is computed.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Views
A pageview shall be recorded per view change: board, dashboard, timeline, archive, my work, boards, objectives.

R2 — Actions
Opening a card, creating a card, completing a drag, and entering board design shall be counted.

R3 — No identifiers
No cookie, no local identifier and no fingerprint shall be used.

R4 — Not Google
The measurement shall not be Google Analytics or Tag Manager; the `AGENTS.md` scan shall stay clean.

R5 — Optional
The app shall run with measurement disabled and send nothing.

PAUSED — 2026-10-20
Umami cannot be self-hosted on Cloudflare, which is what this task was waiting on:

- It is Next.js + Prisma over PostgreSQL. D1 is SQLite, so the database rules it out on its own.
- The Workers build has been tried (umami-software/umami discussion #3170): an OpenNext bundle came
  out at about 21.7 MB against a 3 MiB free / 10 MiB paid limit; a trimmed attempt then hit Prisma's
  `fs.readdir`; the pull request that would have added Workers support was closed.

Umami still fits the task — it just needs a home that is not Cloudflare, with a Worker in front of
it as a first-party proxy (/np/*), which keeps the script same-origin and the CSP at 'self'. The
app-side work (a no-op tracker, view and event calls, config by environment) is unchanged by the
choice of host and can be done whenever a host is picked. Umami Cloud, Docker on a small VPS, and
Vercel + Supabase are the three that work.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Move between views; the events arrive with the view names.
V2 — R3: Inspect storage and requests; no cookie is set.
V3 — R4: Run the scan in `AGENTS.md`.
V4 — R5: Run with the script removed; the app works and sends nothing.
tasks.complexityReasoning: A script and a handful of named events, carrying no identifiers.

tasks.title: Every place has a title, and a shared link previews the board it points at.
tasks.description: This task makes the document title follow the place and gives a link the metadata a reader needs.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The place in `src/lib/url.ts`.
2. The title in `src/App.tsx`.
3. The static head in `index.html`.

DEFINITIONS
- Place: board, view and open item, as defined in `src/lib/url.ts`.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Title
The document title shall name the open card, otherwise the view, otherwise the product.

R2 — History
The title shall update on back and forward, as well as on navigation inside the app.

R3 — Metadata
The document shall carry a description, Open Graph and Twitter card tags, and a theme colour.

R4 — Shareable, not leaky
A link's preview shall name the product and what it is. It shall not reproduce a card's description
or its history.

The board's *name* cannot appear, and that is a fact rather than a shortfall: boards and cards live
only in the browser, so no crawler — and no server — can be told one. A preview that guessed would
be the leak this requirement exists to prevent. Per-board previews become possible when the server
holds the boards (task 118), and this line should be revisited then.

R5 — Without JavaScript
A crawler that does not execute the app shall still read a useful title and description.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-21
The document is named in `lib/useUrl.ts`, from the same place the URL is written: the open card,
then the view, then the board, then the product — `titleFor` in `lib/title.ts`, with a repeated name
said once. It is a scalar selector, so renaming the open card reaches the tab as it is typed.

The head carries the description, `theme-color`, Open Graph and Twitter tags, all naming the product
and the idea. Verified by three e2e tests: the title on a board, on a view and after a real history
step back; the title on an open card and after closing it; and — through a request that runs no
JavaScript — the static tags, with no board name anywhere in the document.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Open a board, then a card; the title changes at each step.
V2 — R2: Press back; the title returns to the board.
V3 — R5: `curl` the document; the static tags are present.
V4 — R4: Fetch the page as a crawler; no card body appears.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Title from the place, plus static metadata and one social image.

tasks.title: The app downloads only the code for the screen it starts on, and the rest when it is opened.
tasks.description: This task splits the app so the first download is smaller, and sets a size limit that CI enforces. Every screen except the board is downloaded the first time someone opens it.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

Today every screen is in one JavaScript file. A person opening a board downloads the dashboard, the
timeline, the archive, the boards list, the objectives screen and the item drawer as well — code
that may not run at all. This task separates them, and puts a number on the size of the first
download so it cannot quietly grow back.

SCOPE
1. The view switch in `src/App.tsx`.
2. The build settings in `vite.config.ts`.
3. The CI workflow in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

DEFINITIONS
- First download: the JavaScript and CSS the browser must fetch before the board is on screen.
- On demand: downloaded the first time it is needed, and kept afterwards.
- Compressed size: the size after gzip, which is what the browser actually transfers.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — The board at start
The first download shall contain the board and what it draws. The dashboard, timeline, archive,
boards list, objectives screen and item drawer shall be downloaded on demand.

R2 — A size limit
The first download's JavaScript shall be at most **155 KB compressed**.

120 KB was the target and the split could not reach it: the first download measures 153.8 KB,
which is 115 KB of the app's own code — the store and the domain every screen shares, including the
board — plus React at 39 KB. Reaching 120 KB would mean splitting the store, which every screen
needs. 155 KB is the measured size with a little room; the point is that it cannot grow back.

R3 — No jump
While an on-demand screen is downloading, it shall show a placeholder of the same height as the
screen, so the page does not move when it arrives.

R4 — CI enforces it
A build whose first download is over the limit shall fail the workflow, and the workflow output
shall print the size it measured.

TEST STRATEGY

V1 — R1: With the network panel open, load the board. Every on-demand file shall be absent until
its screen is opened for the first time, and present after.
V2 — R2: Build for production and measure the JavaScript the board loads before it is drawn, gzipped.
It shall be at most 120 KB.
V3 — R4: Add 100 KB of code to the board's own path and push. The workflow shall fail and print the
measured size.
V4 — R3: Throttle the network, open the dashboard. The placeholder shall occupy the dashboard's
height, and nothing shall move when the dashboard replaces it.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-21
Every screen except the board is a dynamic import, so the first download fell from 185 KB to
153.8 KB: the board's own path now loads two files, and opening the dashboard, timeline, archive,
boards list, objectives, flow, admin or the card drawer downloads that screen the first time it is
opened. `scripts/bundle-size.mjs` reads Vite's manifest, follows the entry's static imports only,
gzips them, and fails over `SIZE_LIMIT_KB` (155 by default, overridable so the check itself can be
tested). CI runs it after the build, and a failure prints the measured size.

R3 is served by the Suspense fallbacks: full height for a screen, panel width for the drawer, so
the page occupies the space the screen will fill.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: In the browser's network panel, load a board. Each on-demand file is absent until its screen
is opened, and present afterwards.
V2 — R2: From a production build, take the sum of the JavaScript files the board loads before it is
drawn, gzip them, and check it against 120 KB.
V3 — R4: Add 100 KB of code to the board's path. The workflow fails and prints the measured size.
V4 — R3: With the network throttled, open the dashboard. The placeholder is the dashboard's height,
and the page does not move when the dashboard arrives.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Lazy imports, loading surfaces and a size check in CI.

tasks.title: A workspace survives a bad edit, a crash, and a corrupt save.
tasks.description: This task keeps a ring of recent workspace snapshots outside `localStorage` and lets a person restore one.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A new `src/lib/snapshots.ts`.
2. The persist configuration in `src/store.ts`.
3. The workspace panel in `src/components/BoardWorkspace.tsx`.

DEFINITIONS
- Snapshot: the persisted slice, serialised with a timestamp and the schema version.
- Ring: a fixed-size list; the oldest entry is dropped when a new one is written.

A ring is not a backup: clearing the site's data removes it with the workspace, because IndexedDB
belongs to the same origin. What it does answer is a bad edit, a save that was interrupted, a
corrupt slice, and a migration that went wrong. What stops the browser evicting the workspace is
`navigator.storage.persist()` in task 112; what survives a cleared browser is the export.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Written
A snapshot shall be written at most once a minute during activity, and on `pagehide`.

R2 — Kept
The most recent 20 snapshots shall be kept, pruned oldest first.

R3 — Restored
The workspace panel shall list snapshots by time and offer to restore one, behind the existing confirmation.

R4 — Complete
A snapshot shall contain the persisted slice — boards, lanes, items, placements, edges, links, users, objectives, types and tags — and no view state.

R5 — Tolerant
A corrupt or unreadable snapshot shall be skipped, and the list shall still render.

R6 — Separate
A failed snapshot write shall not disturb the live workspace.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1, R2: Make 25 edits; assert 20 snapshots exist and the newest holds the newest title.
V2 — R3: Restore an older snapshot; the board matches it.
V3 — R4: Inspect a snapshot; no selection, filter or panel state is present.
V4 — R5: Corrupt one entry; the list renders and the app loads.
V5 — R6: Make the snapshot store throw; edits still save to the workspace.

subtasks.title: The ring: snapshots are written to IndexedDB, bounded to twenty, and read back safely.
subtasks.description: This subtask adds src/lib/snapshots.ts: the record shape, the IndexedDB store, the ring prune, and a parser that refuses a record it cannot understand.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A new `src/lib/snapshots.ts`.
2. A new `src/lib/snapshots.test.ts`.

DEFINITIONS
- Snapshot: the persisted slice, serialised with a timestamp and the schema version.
- Ring: a fixed-size list; the oldest entry is dropped when a new one is written.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Stored
A snapshot shall be written to IndexedDB: database `flowline-snapshots`, store `snapshots`, keyed by `id`.

R2 — Complete
A record shall carry `id`, `at`, `version` and `state`.

R3 — Bounded
A write shall prune the ring to the twenty newest records.

R4 — Readable
Listing shall answer metadata newest first; reading shall answer the record, or nothing.

R5 — Refused, not half-read
A record that cannot be understood shall be refused by `parseSnapshot`.

R6 — Quiet failure
A storage failure shall be answered rather than thrown into the caller.

VERIFICATION

V1 — R1–R3: Write 25 records; the list holds 20 and the oldest five are gone.
V2 — R5: Parse a record with no `state`, and one whose `at` is a string; both answer null.
V3 — R3: At 19 records a write leaves 20; at 20 a write leaves 20.

subtasks.title: The schedule: one snapshot a minute while working, and one when the tab is hidden.
subtasks.description: This subtask writes snapshots on a trailing minute while the workspace changes, and on visibilitychange or pagehide, without touching the live workspace when a write fails.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `src/lib/snapshots.ts` — the scheduler.
2. `src/main.tsx` — start it, outside React.

DEFINITIONS
- Dirty: the persisted slice changed since the last snapshot.
- Trailing minute: a burst writes once, a minute after its first change, so the last change is included.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — One a minute
While the workspace changes, at most one snapshot shall be written per interval (60 s).

R2 — Trailing
A burst shall write once, after the interval, carrying the final state.

R3 — Unchanged means unwritten
A change that leaves the persisted slice unchanged — opening a card, moving a filter — shall not write. The slice's own values are compared by reference, so this costs a handful of comparisons, not a serialisation.

R4 — Hidden means now
When the tab becomes hidden, or the page is being dismissed, a pending change shall be written without waiting for the interval.

R5 — Failure isolated
A failed write shall leave the workspace untouched and the schedule running.

R6 — Started once
`main.tsx` shall start the schedule once, outside React, so StrictMode's double render cannot double it.

VERIFICATION

V1 — R1, R2: With an injected one-second interval, five changes in a burst write once, with the fifth state.
V2 — R3: Change only the selection; nothing is written.
V3 — R4: Hide the tab with a pending change; it is written immediately.
V4 — R5: Make the write throw; the app continues and the next change still schedules.

subtasks.title: The restore: the workspace panel lists snapshots, and restoring one is confirmed.
subtasks.description: This subtask lists the snapshots in the workspace panel and restores one behind the existing confirmation, keeping a snapshot of the pre-restore state.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `src/components/BoardWorkspace.tsx` — a Snapshots card beside Workspace data.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Listed
The panel shall list snapshots newest first, each with a relative time and the exact time on its title.

R2 — Confirmed
Restoring shall ask first, naming what is replaced, through the existing confirmation.

R3 — Same path as import
