Restoring shall call `importWorkspace(state, version)` — the path the file import already uses.

R4 — Undoable
Before restoring, a snapshot of the current workspace shall be written, so the restore can itself be undone.

R5 — Unreadable is refused
A snapshot that cannot be read shall be reported, and shall replace nothing.

subtasks.title: A snapshot carries the workspace and nothing about the view.
subtasks.description: This subtask proves a snapshot is the persisted slice and no selection, filter, multi-select or panel state.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Slice only
A snapshot's `state` shall be `persistedSlice`: no selection, filters, multi-select, confirm, panel, menu or drag state.

R2 — Versioned
The record shall carry `PERSIST_VERSION`.

R3 — Restorable as it stands
A slice written at the current version shall be accepted by `importWorkspace` without a migration.

VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Snapshot the fixture; assert no view key is present and every persisted key is.
V2 — R3: Import that snapshot into a reset store; the boards, cards and titles match.

subtasks.title: The ring is proved in a browser: bounds, restore, corruption, a failed write.
subtasks.description: This subtask exercises the ring in a real browser: twenty-five edits leave twenty snapshots, an older restore matches, a corrupt entry is skipped and the list still renders, and a failing write leaves the app working.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

VERIFICATION

V1 — 25 edits leave 20 snapshots, and the newest holds the newest title.
V2 — Restoring an older snapshot makes the board match it.
V3 — A corrupted record is skipped and the list still renders.
V4 — A failing write leaves the app working, and the next edit still schedules.
V5 — Hiding the tab writes a pending change without waiting for the interval.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Split into: (1) the snapshot store — serialise the persisted slice, write the ring, prune to 20, tolerate corrupt entries; (2) the schedule (trailing minute and pagehide) and isolation from the live workspace; (3) the restore surface in the workspace panel behind the existing confirmation; (4) tests: ring bounds, restore fidelity, a corrupt entry, a failed write.
tasks.complexityReasoning: IndexedDB, a ring with pruning, a restore surface behind confirmation, tolerance for corrupt entries, and isolation from the live workspace.

tasks.title: The app says when it cannot save, and asks the browser to keep the workspace.
tasks.description: This task makes storage honest: a failed write is surfaced with a way out, and the browser's own promise to keep the data is shown.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The persist storage adapter in `src/store.ts`.
2. The snapshot store from the previous task.
3. The toolbar and the workspace panel.

DEFINITIONS
- Quota failure: a write rejected with `QuotaExceededError`, or a `setItem` that does not store the value.
- Persisted storage: the browser's promise not to evict the origin's storage under pressure.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Detected
A failed write shall be detected rather than assumed to have succeeded.

R2 — Declared
While a write is failing, a persistent banner shall say that changes are not being saved.

R3 — Rescued
The banner shall offer the workspace export in one action.

R4 — Cleared
When a later write succeeds, the banner shall clear when the data is safe again.

R5 — Requested
`navigator.storage.persist()` shall be requested after the first successful save.

R6 — Reported
The workspace panel shall show the storage used and whether it is persistent.

R7 — No false calm
No surface shall indicate a saved state while writes are failing.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1–R3: Mock the storage write to throw; make an edit; the banner appears and the export downloads.
V2 — R4: Restore the write; edit again; the banner clears.
V3 — R5: After the first save, `navigator.storage.persisted()` is true where the browser grants it.
V4 — R6: The panel shows a use figure and the persistence state.
V5 — R7: With the write failing, no saved indicator is shown.
tasks.expansionPrompt: (1) the storage adapter that detects and reports a failed write; (2) the banner — appears while failing, clears when safe — and its export action; (3) persist()/estimate() and the workspace-panel read-out; (4) mock-driven tests for each state.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Detecting a rejected write is subtler than it looks: `setItem` can fail at quota, so the adapter must verify. Then a banner state machine, persist()/estimate(), and mocks.

tasks.title: Two browser tabs show one workspace, and neither silently overwrites the other.
tasks.description: This task makes browser tabs share their changes and refuse to clobber a newer one. A "tab" here is a browser tab on the app\u2019s origin \u2014 not one of the app\u2019s own views.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The persist layer in `src/store.ts`.
2. A revision guard on the persisted slice.
3. A channel between browser tabs: the `storage` event, which the browser fires in every other tab, and `BroadcastChannel` where it exists.

DEFINITIONS
- Revision: a monotonically increasing identifier of the persisted slice.
- Stale tab: a tab holding a revision older than the stored one.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Propagated
A write in one tab shall reach another tab within a second.

R2 — Checked
A tab shall compare its revision with the stored one before writing.

R3 — Refused
A stale tab shall not overwrite the newer slice.

R4 — Explained
A stale tab shall say that the workspace changed elsewhere, and shall offer to reload.

R5 — View state stays local
The reconciliation shall not merge selection, filters, multi-select or panel state between tabs.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Two tabs; rename a board in one; the other shows the new name.
V2 — R2, R3: Hold a stale copy in one tab; edit; the newer workspace is unchanged.
V3 — R4: The stale tab shows the notice, and reload brings it up to date.
V4 — R5: Different views in two tabs; changing the view in one does not move the other.
tasks.expansionPrompt: (1) the revision in the persisted slice and the guard before a write; (2) the BroadcastChannel/storage channel and reconciliation; (3) the stale-tab notice and reload; (4) two-tab tests.
tasks.complexityReasoning: A revision guard on every write, two tabs kept coherent, and a stale tab that refuses rather than clobbers, without merging view state.

tasks.title: A schema change never replaces someone's workspace with the demo.
tasks.description: This task changes the migration policy from reseeding to preserving and refusing, so an unmigratable workspace is never silently replaced.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `migratePersisted` and `migrateState` in `src/store.ts`.
2. The import and restore surfaces.

DEFINITIONS
- Known version: a persisted version this build can migrate.
- Unknown or corrupt state: a version or shape this build cannot read.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Migrated
A workspace at a known older version shall be migrated, never reseeded.

R2 — Preserved
A workspace that cannot be migrated shall be copied, unmodified, to a named backup key before anything else happens.

R3 — Refused
The app shall not present an unmigratable slice as the person's workspace.

R4 — Offered
The person shall be offered the preserved data as a download.

R5 — No silent seed
The demo workspace shall not replace existing persisted data.

R6 — Explained
The refusal shall name the version found and the version this build reads.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Load a fixture stamped with an older known version; the boards match after load.
V2 — R2, R3, R5: Load a corrupt slice; the backup key exists and the demo is not shown as their workspace.
V3 — R4: The download action produces the preserved slice.
V4 — R6: The message names both versions.
tasks.expansionPrompt: (1) preserve to a backup key before any migration is attempted; (2) refuse-and-explain in the boot path; (3) the download offer; (4) tests for a known, an unknown and a corrupt version.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Small code on the data-loss path: migration must preserve, refuse and offer rather than reseed. High consequence, not high volume.

tasks.title: Every change to an item goes through one write path, and each item carries a revision.
tasks.description: This task introduces the seam that a lock and a sync will need, without changing behaviour.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The item mutators in `src/store.ts` (about twenty).
2. `Item` in `src/domain/types.ts`.

DEFINITIONS
- Seam: the single helper through which item changes are written.
- Revision: a counter on an item, incremented once per accepted change.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — One path
Every item mutation shall write through one helper.

R2 — Revision
An accepted change to an item shall increment that item's `rev` exactly once.

R3 — Optional
`rev` shall be optional, so existing persisted items read without a migration.

R4 — No behaviour change
The existing tests shall pass unchanged.

R5 — Enumerated
A test shall enumerate the item mutators and assert that each goes through the seam and bumps `rev`.

R6 — Placements excluded
A placement change shall not bump the item's `rev`.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-21
`writeItems(state, change)` is the one content write path: it maps the change and bumps the
revision of every item whose object changed, by reference — exact, and cheap. Seventeen content
sites go through it. The eight placement actions, `placeCard`'s Done stamp and the seam's own map
are the only raw item maps left, and are arrangement rather than content: a move still writes the
item's log, it just is not a revision.

`rev` is optional, so the fixture — old data — reads with no migration and revises from one.

R5 is met twice over: a table of sixteen content mutators asserts each bumps its item by exactly
one, and a structural test counts the raw item maps in `store.ts` (ten) so a new write cannot
quietly skip the seam. Both were proved by breaking them: a bypassing write made the count test
fail, and the table fails by name for a mutator that stops bumping.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1, R2: Edit a title twice; `rev` is 2.
V2 — R3: Load an item with no `rev`; the app renders and an edit sets it.
V3 — R4: `npm test`.
V4 — R5: Add a mutator that bypasses the seam; the enumeration test fails.
V5 — R6: Move a card between lanes; its `rev` is unchanged.
tasks.expansionPrompt: (1) the write helper and `rev` on Item, optional; (2) move every item mutator onto it, one action at a time, with the suite green after each; (3) the enumeration test that fails if a mutator bypasses the seam; (4) confirm placements do not bump `rev`.
tasks.complexityReasoning: A mechanical refactor of about twenty mutators and twenty-one write sites that must change nothing, plus an enumeration test to keep the seam honest. Regression risk rather than conceptual difficulty.

tasks.title: A change says who made it.
tasks.description: This task records the author on every new log entry and shows it in the Activity tab.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `ItemLogEntry` in `src/domain/types.ts`.
2. The log helper in `src/store.ts`.
3. The Activity rows in `src/components/ItemPanel.tsx`.

DEFINITIONS
- Author: the identity that made the change.
- Unknown identity: no author recorded, rather than a guess.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Recorded
A new log entry shall carry the author.

R2 — Optional
An entry written before this change shall render unchanged.

R3 — Shown
The Activity row shall name the author beside the time.

R4 — Not invented
Where the identity is unknown, the entry shall omit the author.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-21
`ItemLogEntry.by` is optional, and every entry is stamped where it is made: `logEntry` and
`movedEntry` both read a single mirror of `meUserId`, kept in step by a subscription on the store
rather than set at each door — a copy set at every entry point could fall out of step, and a wrong
author is worse than none. Absent when nobody has said who they are.

The Activity row names the author beside the time, and says only the time for an entry from before
identities existed: a name there would be invented.

Three unit tests (stamped, omitted, a move stamped too, old entries untouched) and one e2e that
drives the real control: My work's "Whose work to show", then a rename, then the Activity names
Maya Blake.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Make an edit; the newest entry carries the author.
V2 — R2: Load a fixture with older entries; the panel renders.
V3 — R4: Clear the identity; the new entry has no author.
tasks.complexityReasoning: A field on the log entry, stamped by the seam, and one row of display.

tasks.title: A person signs in with the account they already have — Google or Microsoft.
tasks.description: This task adds accounts: two sign-on providers, a session, invitations and sign-out — no passwords and no codes.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. An identity provider that takes provider registrations rather than a bespoke OAuth client:
   Supabase Auth, or Better Auth if the database decision goes another way.
2. A provider registry: Google and Microsoft are the hosted defaults, and a deployment may
   configure others — an OIDC issuer of its own, or email — without a code change.
3. `meUserId` in `src/store.ts`, which stops being a local pointer and becomes a real identity.

DEFINITIONS
- Provider: an outside service that vouches for an email address, with the person's consent.
- Session: the credential that survives a reload and ends on sign-out.
- Verified address: the address a provider has confirmed. It is what joins two doors to one person.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Sign in with a provider
A person shall sign in with Google or with Microsoft, in one step, without a password and without a
code.

R2 — The providers are configuration
The set of providers shall be configuration, not code. The hosted instance ships Google and
Microsoft; a self-hosted one may configure a different set — including an OIDC issuer of its own,
or email — without a code change. At least one provider that is not Google shall be available in
every configuration, so someone with a Microsoft account and no Google account can use the app, and
the reverse. The app shall start in development with no provider configured.

R3 — One person, two doors
A person who signs in with the same verified address by either provider shall reach the same
account, not two.

R4 — Session
A session shall survive a reload, expire after a recorded period, and end on sign-out.

R5 — Invitation
Inviting an address shall create a pending member, accepted when that address first signs in by
either provider.

R6 — Consent, narrowly
The clients shall ask for an email address and nothing else, and shall not request access to mail,
files, contacts or a calendar.

R7 — Limited
Starting a sign-in and the callback shall be rate limited, and the callback shall check its state
parameter so a crafted link cannot complete a sign-in.

R8 — Optional in development
The app shall run with no provider configured, and never fail to start because one is missing.

R9 — A way to be someone else in development
Development shall offer a way to act as a named identity without a provider. The tests that matter
most — two people on one board — need two identities, and a self-hosted instance needs someone able
to sign in before any provider has been configured.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
Accounts live on the server seam rather than in a provider's own service, so the same routes run on
Cloudflare and on a self-hosted machine. `server/auth/` holds the registry, the OAuth flow (code and
PKCE, a state bound to the browser, `userinfo` for the address), sessions (an HttpOnly cookie; the
table holds only the token's hash), invitations, and the development switch.

The provider list is configuration. Google and Microsoft are enabled by their client credentials, and
`AUTH_OIDC_*` adds an identity provider of the instance's own without a code change. An instance with
none configured offers no sign-in and is still a working board.

One person is one account: two providers naming the same verified address join rather than make a
second, and an address the provider will not vouch for is refused. The first person to arrive owns
the instance; an invited address arrives with the role the invitation gave; the invitation is spent.

The client offers sign-in only when the instance does. It renders nothing otherwise, which is why
`dist/` still works on any host with no server at all.

Evidence: fifteen unit tests over the registry, the flow against a fake provider, linking,
invitations, sign-out, the flood cap and the switch; an end-to-end test that signs in against the
Node entry, reloads, and signs out. `npm run smoke:node` passes with the new migration.

KNOWN, DELIBERATE: while the workspace is still local, an account is matched to the workspace's own
person by display name. Task 118 replaces that guess with a record.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Sign in with Google on a laptop. Sign out. Sign in with Microsoft on the same laptop. Both
reach the workspace.
V2 — R2: Configure only the Microsoft client, and sign in. Repeat with only the Google client. Run
the app with neither, and confirm it starts and says sign-in is not configured.
V3 — R3: Sign in with Google as an address, sign out, sign in with Microsoft as the same verified
address. It is the same account, not a second one.
V4 — R4: Reload; still signed in. Sign out; the session is gone, and the back button does not bring
it back.
V5 — R5: Invite an address; sign in with it by either provider; the membership is active.
V6 — R6: Inspect the consent screen. The scopes are the address and nothing more.
V7 — R7: Start a sign-in with a forged state parameter; it is refused. Repeat the callback quickly;
it is rate limited.
tasks.expansionPrompt: (1) provider and sending domain — SPF, DKIM, DMARC on a subdomain; (2) the code and link flow with a session; (3) invitations and first-sign-in acceptance; (4) rate limits and spent-code refusal; (5) the optional Google provider, off by default.
tasks.complexityReasoning: The code is ordinary; the operational surface is not: email deliverability (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), rate limits, invitations, and a provider choice coupled to the database.

tasks.title: The workspace lives on the server, and the browser holds a cache of it.
tasks.description: This task moves the record of truth to the server behind one boundary, with an offline queue and a first-sign-in import.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A database schema for boards, lanes, items, placements, edges, links, users, types, tags, objectives and logs.
2. An API over that schema.
3. A repository adapter behind `src/store.ts`.
4. First-sign-in import of the local workspace.
5. A portable server: one `fetch` handler, two entries (Workers and Node), and one database
   interface over SQLite.

DEFINITIONS
- Authority: the copy that survives a cleared browser.
- Queue: accepted writes not yet acknowledged by the server.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Server is the record
The server shall be authoritative; the browser shall hold a cache.

R2 — One boundary
The store shall read and write through one adapter, so that the local and server builds differ only there.

R3 — Optimistic
A write shall apply locally at once, and reconcile with the server's answer.

R4 — Offline
Accepted writes made offline shall queue and be sent once, in order, on reconnect.

R5 — Import
First sign-in shall offer to import the local workspace, without losing items, edges, placements, logs, types, tags or objectives.

R6 — Live
A change on one device shall reach another without a reload.

R7 — Refused, not dropped
A write the server cannot apply shall be refused and surfaced.

R8 — Migrated
The server schema shall be migrated with the discipline `PERSIST_VERSION` uses.

R9 — Portable, from the first table
The API shall be a `fetch` handler, run by a Worker on Cloudflare and by a Node process for a
self-hosted instance, so the two deployments differ only in their entry file and their bindings —
never in a route, a query or a rule. The schema shall be SQLite, which is what D1 is, so one set of
migrations serves both. CI shall boot both entries.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1, R6: Two devices; edit on one; the other updates.
V2 — R3: The local edit appears before the server answers.
V3 — R4: Disconnect; make three edits; reconnect; three writes, applied once each.
V4 — R5: Import the demo workspace; counts match for every entity and the logs are intact.
V5 — R7: Force a stale write; it is refused and reported.
V6 — R8: Apply a migration; rows written before it still read.

subtasks.title: The schema and the read: the server holds a workspace and can hand it back.
subtasks.description: This subtask adds the D1 schema for every entity the store persists, and one endpoint that returns the whole workspace.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A SQLite database (`flowline-workspace` on D1, a file on a self-hosted instance), its
   migrations, and `POST /api/workspace` reads.
2. A schema mirrored from `persistedSlice`: boards, lanes, items, placements, edges, links, users,
   issue types, tags, objectives, key results, board templates.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Every entity
Every entity the browser persists shall have a table, and nothing else shall be invented.

R2 — One read
A client shall be able to fetch the whole workspace in one request, shaped exactly as
`persistedSlice` is, so the store can take it without a translation layer.

R3 — Ambition is not scope
The first version shall be a read. It proves the schema and the shape; writes are the next step.

R4 — Behind the session
The endpoint shall answer only a signed-in member of the workspace (task 117), and nothing at all
without one.

R5 — Migrated
The schema shall be created by migrations, not by hand — the same rule the browser's schema follows.

R6 — SQLite, not a vendor
The schema and every statement shall be plain SQLite, reached through one `Database` interface with
two implementations — D1 in the hosted deployment, a file driver in a self-hosted one. No statement
shall depend on an API only one of them has, and none shall use what D1 refuses: `ATTACH`, extension
loading, or a restricted pragma. The schema shall be exercised on both before it is depended on.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`migrations/0003_workspace.sql` holds every entity the browser persists: people, issue types,
boards, board kinds and tags, lanes, items, checklists, item history, placements, edges, links,
objectives, key results, board templates and their lanes, and the settings row. An array of
references — tags, assignees, linked boards — is JSON in its row, because a reference is not a
thing the workspace owns.

`server/workspace/read.ts` answers the whole workspace in one request, shaped exactly as
`persistedSlice`. `server/workspace/write.ts` replaces the whole workspace in one transaction — the
seed for 118.3 and for the first-sign-in import in 118.6, and what makes the round-trip test
possible.

Two things worth recording:
- **A person is not an account.** `users` is the account table from 0002; the workspace's people are
  `people`. An assignee need never sign in, and an account need never be assigned anything.
- **The read is a GET**, not the POST the scope line said: it has no body and changes nothing.

Evidence: a round-trip test (a workspace with a three-deep lane tree, both edge kinds, an item with
history and a checklist, a template, saved filters) goes in through the writer and comes back
identical through the endpoint; an empty database reads as empty rather than broken; a request
without a session is 401 and one from a non-member is 403.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`src/lib/repository.ts` is the one interface the store persists through, and `chooseRepository` is
the one place an adapter is chosen. The store no longer names `localStorage`, `guardedStorage` or
`tabSynced`: `src/store.ts` asks for a repository and gives `persist` its storage.

The local adapter is the shipped behaviour exactly, and the tests say so rather than assuming it:
the slice passes through unreshaped with its revision beside it, a failed write is published instead
of thrown, and the e2e suite is unchanged.

The server adapter is not written here, deliberately. A repository that could read a server
workspace but not save one would lose the first edit, so it arrives with the write path in 118.3 —
and this interface is what it will be written against. R2 says "two adapters"; the honest count
today is one, and a second that cannot keep a change would be worse than none.

subtasks.title: One boundary: the store reads and writes through an adapter, and the local build is unchanged.
subtasks.description: This subtask puts a repository behind the store, with a local adapter that keeps today's behaviour and an HTTP one for the server.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `src/lib/repository.ts` — one interface the store reads and writes through.
2. Two adapters: `local` (today's behaviour) and `http` (the server).

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — One boundary
The store shall reach persistence through one interface, so the local and server builds differ only
in which adapter they are given.

R2 — Unchanged locally
With the local adapter the app shall behave exactly as it does today: the existing unit tests and
the e2e suite pass without a change.

R3 — Not a second model
The adapter shall carry the persisted slice as it is. It shall not introduce a second shape the
store has to understand.

R4 — Chosen once
Which adapter is used shall be decided in one place — a build flag or the presence of a session —
rather than scattered through the app.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`src/lib/repository.ts` is the one interface the store persists through, and `chooseRepository` is
the one place an adapter is chosen. The local adapter is the shipped behaviour exactly, with tests
that say so; the server adapter arrived with the write path in 118.3.

subtasks.title: The write path: a change goes to the server with the revision it was based on.
subtasks.description: This subtask sends one entity's change at a time, applies it locally at once, and refuses a write the server has moved past.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The write endpoints, and the seam in `store.ts` (`writeItems`, task 115).
2. The client's optimistic apply and the server's answer.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Optimistic
A change shall apply locally at once, so typing is never waiting on a network.

R2 — Revisioned
Every write shall carry the `rev` it was based on, which the seam already keeps per item.

R3 — Refused, not dropped
A write the server has moved past shall be refused and surfaced (409), never applied and never
silently discarded — the same rule the card lease later leans on.

R4 — One entity at a time
The first entity through the path shall be the item, because the seam is where it is written. The
rest follow the same shape once the item path is proved.

R5 — No second truth
When the server answers, its version is the one kept — the client does not merge by hand.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`PATCH /api/workspace/items/:id` takes a card with the revision it was based on, checks it against
the stored one, and keeps that plus one — so the server owns the revision and the client is never
asked to merge. A change based on a revision the workspace has moved past is 409 with the version
that is there now; an item the server has never seen is a creation, because a disagreement about a
version needs a version to disagree about. Nothing is applied on refusal, and nothing is dropped in
silence.

The client sends from `writeItems`, the seam task 115 made: the change is in the store before
anything is sent, one write at a time and in the order the changes were made, because typing is many
changes each based on the one before. The answer is adopted when it differs, and a refusal is
published in the toolbar with the card it was about rather than swallowed.

The repository grew `commitItem`. The local adapter answers "kept" without sending anything; the
http one sends and reads the answer. `chooseRepository` decides at call time from the session, so the
same build is both deployments — this is the adapter 118.2 deliberately did not write.

Deliberately not here: the offline queue (118.4), so an unreachable server says so and the local
change stands; and the words of a refused edit are not yet kept for the person to act on (121).

subtasks.title: The offline queue: accepted changes wait, go once, and go in order.
subtasks.description: This subtask keeps writes made offline in a queue with an idempotency key, flushed on reconnect.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A queue of accepted writes, and the reconnect path.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Accepted only
A write refused by the server shall never be queued. Replaying a refusal is the lost update the
revision exists to prevent.

R2 — In order
Queued writes shall be sent in the order they were made, so the workspace on the server is never
a state the person did not pass through.

R3 — Once
Every queued write shall carry an idempotency key, so a retry after a lost response cannot apply
the same change twice.

R4 — Reconnect
A dropped connection shall resume the queue without a reload, and the person shall see that writes
are waiting rather than assuming they landed.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
A change the server could not answer is held in `src/lib/queue.ts`, in the order it was made, with
the revision it was based on and a key that names the change rather than the attempt. It survives a
reload because it is stored, it is bounded at 500 entries so a week offline cannot fill the disk, and
when it is full the toolbar says so rather than dropping the oldest work.

`flushQueue` sends it in order and removes an entry only when the server has answered it — applied or
refused — so a refusal is never retried, which is what keeps a queue from becoming a lost update. It
stops at the first answer that does not arrive, so the order is never rearranged around a gap, and it
resumes on `online` or on a five-second retry, because a server that went away is not a network
interface that changed.

`PATCH /api/workspace/items/:id` takes a `key` and records it in the same batch as the change it
names, so a retry after a lost response is answered with what is stored instead of applied twice. The
table prunes itself after a day.

The toolbar counts what is waiting. The e2e signs in, opens a card, drops the connection, renames it,
sees "N waiting", reconnects, and finds the title on the server with no reload and no button.

subtasks.title: Live: a change on one device arrives on another without a reload.
subtasks.description: This subtask opens a channel per workspace and pushes changes down it, with no echo back to the writer.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A channel per workspace, behind one interface: a Durable Object on Cloudflare, a WebSocket server
   on the Node entry, and a poll of the revision on an instance that has neither.
2. The client's subscription, and the store's adoption of what arrives.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Live
A change saved by one device shall reach another without a reload.

R2 — No echo
The tab that wrote shall not receive its own change back as news, and two tabs shall not answer
each other for ever — the lesson from task 113.

R3 — The same channel the lease will use
The workspace lease (task 120) needs a live connection too. This shall be that connection, not a
second one beside it.

R4 — Behind the session
A connection shall belong to a signed-in member of the workspace and no one else.

R5 — Portable
The channel shall sit behind one interface, so a self-hosted instance with no Durable Objects still
delivers a change — through its own WebSocket server, or by polling the revision. CI shall exercise
the fallback, not only the Durable Object.

PROGRESS — 2026-10-22
The feed and the fallback are built; the two push transports are not, and this task stays open until
they are.

WHAT IS THERE
`GET /api/workspace/changes?since=…` reads a `changes` table written in the same batch as the item
it announces, so a change that landed is a change that is announced. It pages at fifty, dedupes to
the latest revision per card — the feed says *what* changed, not every step — and sits behind the
same guard as the read.

The client polls it every two seconds while the tab is visible, catches up when it is looked at, and
sits behind `poll`/`startLive`/`stopLive` so a push transport can replace the timing without moving
the cursor or the shape. An arriving card is adopted only when its revision is greater, which is
also what makes an echo a no-op: the tab that wrote already holds that revision, sets no state and
writes nothing back — the lesson task 113 taught.

An e2e signs two contexts in, edits a card in one, and waits for the other to show it, never
navigating the second page.

WHAT IS NOT
The WebSocket server on the Node entry, and the Durable Object on Cloudflare. Both are optimisations
over a feed that already works on both runtimes — a self-hosted instance and the hosted one are both
live within two seconds — so R1-R4 hold today. R5's "CI shall exercise the fallback, not only the
Durable Object" is true by construction, because the fallback is what runs; the sentence still
assumes a push transport exists, and it does not yet.

subtasks.title: First sign-in: a local workspace can become the account's workspace.
subtasks.description: This subtask offers the browser's workspace at first sign-in and imports it without losing anything.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. First sign-in, and the import of the browser's workspace.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Offered, not taken
A person with a local workspace shall be asked, once, whether to bring it.

R2 — Complete
Importing shall preserve every entity and every log, including `rev` and the entries' authors.

R3 — One workspace
After importing, the account's workspace shall be the one the person was working in — not a merge
of two, and not an empty one beside it.

R4 — Undoable
The local workspace shall not be deleted by the import; the export remains until the person says
otherwise.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`POST /api/workspace/import` takes the browser's whole workspace and writes it in one transaction,
replacing rather than merging — R3's "not two half-workspaces beside each other". It refuses a
workspace that already has a board (409), refuses anything that is not a workspace (400), and sits
behind the same guard as every other write. The parser keeps what it can: an item it cannot read is
dropped, and the boards around it are still worth importing.

`ImportNotice` offers it where the account is, once: only when this browser has boards and the
account has none, and only until the person accepts or declines. Accepting copies; it does not move.
The local workspace is untouched, so a failed import costs nothing and R4 holds — the export stays.

The e2e signs in on an instance with no boards, sees the offer, copies, and finds the boards on the
server while the board keeps drawing.

STILL MISSING, AND NOT IN THIS TASK'S WORDS
The browser reads the account's workspace only through the change feed's cards and a first-sign-in
check. There is no "load the workspace from the server" path, so a second device shows its own seed
rather than the account's boards until something tells it otherwise. That is the read half of
118.2's adapter, which was written for the local case and extended for writes in 118.3 — the read
side is the gap, and it is the next thing a person would notice.

subtasks.title: The server's schema migrates with the same discipline as the browser's.
subtasks.description: This subtask gives the server a version and a migration, and a client that refuses rather than guesses when it is behind.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The server's schema version, migrations, and the client's compatibility check.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Versioned
The server's schema shall carry a version, bumped by every change, exactly as `PERSIST_VERSION` is.

R2 — Migrated forward
A migration shall transform existing rows rather than replacing them, and shall be run before the
new code serves a request.

R3 — Refused, not guessed
A client that cannot read what the server returns shall say so, rather than rendering a half
workspace — the browser-side version of the same rule.

R4 — Rehearsed
A migration shall be exercised against a copy of real data before it runs in production.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`schema_migrations` is the server's `PERSIST_VERSION`: one row per migration, written by the
migration itself, so a database migrated by `wrangler d1 migrations apply` and one migrated by the
Node runner agree without either trusting the other's bookkeeping. `0006` creates it and backfills
the five that came before, so an existing database ends where a fresh one does.

`server/migrate.ts` reads what has run, applies what has not, in order, one file to a transaction,
and reports what it did. The Node entry runs it before it serves a request — R2's sentence on the
runtime that can keep it. The code refuses a write, and the full read, against a database below
`REQUIRED_SCHEMA` with a 503 rather than guessing; the two-second change feed is deliberately not
checked, so a poll does not pay for it.

Two numbers, and they are different on purpose: `WORKSPACE_SCHEMA` is the shape of the payload the
client reads (task 118.8 refuses a number it does not know), and `REQUIRED_SCHEMA` is the state of
the schema the code needs. A change to one is not automatically a change to the other.

`scripts/migrate.mjs` is gone: the entry migrates itself, so nothing outside the server has to know
how a database gets its shape, and the e2e and smoke harnesses lost a step each.

R4 is the rehearsal: a database at the shape before the version table, with a board and a card in
it, is migrated and the rows are still the ones that were there. A migration that reseeded would
fail it. A file that throws rolls back and leaves the version where it was, so the next attempt
starts the file again.

subtasks.title: The browser loads the account's workspace, once the queue is empty.
subtasks.description: Signing in on a device shows the account's workspace rather than that device's own seed, and never at the cost of a change that has not been sent.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `reflectAccount` in `src/lib/workspaceSync.ts`.
2. The session path in `src/store.ts`.
3. The `schema` the read answers with.

DEFINITIONS
- Adopt: replace this browser's workspace with the account's, through the file import's own action.
- Held: the queue has a change in it that the server has not answered.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — The account wins when it has something
When the account's workspace has a board, signing in shall show that workspace, not the one this
browser happened to be holding.

R2 — Never over unsent work
Adoption shall not run while the queue holds a change. The queue is the record of work accepted
here, and adopting on top of it would write over exactly that.

R3 — Nothing is taken by guessing
Adopting shall go through the same action as the file import, so validation and the key whitelist
are the same code, and a workspace the app cannot read changes nothing.

R4 — A shape it cannot read is refused
The read shall carry the schema it was written with. A client that does not know that shape shall
say so and show nothing new, rather than half of it.

R5 — One trigger
The decision shall be made in one place — the session subscription — and the component that draws
the offer shall decide nothing.

VERIFICATION
V1 — R1: an instance with boards; a fresh browser signs in; its boards are the account's.
V2 — R2: hold an unsent change, sign in; no adoption, and the change is still held.
V3 — R3: a workspace the parser refuses changes nothing on screen.
V4 — R4: answer with schema 2; the app says it cannot read it and adopts nothing.
V5 — R5: signing in fetches the workspace once, not twice.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`reflectAccount` is one function with one question — what should this browser be showing? — and it
answers `adopted`, `offered`, `held`, `empty`, `mismatch` or `failed`, so the choice is visible to a
test rather than inferred from the screen.

Adoption reuses `importWorkspace`, the file import's own action, so a workspace enters the store one
way and is whitelisted on the way in. It is skipped while the queue holds anything, and it runs only
after `flushQueue` — flush, then look, which is the order that makes the queue meaningful.

`GET /api/workspace` now answers with `schema`, and the client refuses a number it does not know
rather than rendering part of a workspace. The two numbers are deliberately separate — one is what
the server produces, the other what the app understands — and task 118.7 owns moving them together.

The component that draws the offer no longer decides anything: one subscription in the store calls
`reflectAccount`, so signing in makes one request rather than two racing ones.

tasks.title: A backup exists, and someone has restored from it.
tasks.description: This task sets up automated backups and proves a restore works, rather than assuming it does.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The database provider's backup or point-in-time facility.
2. A restore runbook in `docs/`.
3. The workspace export.

DEFINITIONS
- Backup: a copy from which the workspace can be reproduced.
- Restore drill: an actual restore into a scratch environment, compared against a known workspace.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Daily
A full backup shall be taken at least daily.

R2 — Retained
Backups shall be kept for a recorded period, including a copy with another provider.

R3 — Drilled
The team shall restore a backup into a scratch environment and compare it with a known workspace.

R4 — Written down
The runbook shall name the steps, the owner and the date of the last drill.

R5 — Exported
A workspace export shall be available to the person who owns it, on demand.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R3: Restore yesterday's backup; the workspace matches the export taken at the same time.
V2 — R4: `docs/` names the runbook and a recent drill date.
V3 — R1: The provider's schedule is visible and non-zero.
V4 — R5: Export a workspace; the file opens and contains every entity.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Configuration plus a runbook, but the drill is the requirement: a backup nobody has restored is a hope.

tasks.title: One person holds a card's pen at a time.
tasks.description: This task implements the edit lease described in `docs/collaboration.md`: acquisition, heartbeat, expiry, and a read-only drawer for everyone else.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `docs/collaboration.md` (the design).
2. A lock table and its endpoints, plus a workspace channel.
3. `src/components/ItemPanel.tsx`, `src/components/Card.tsx`, the card menu and the bulk bar.
4. `AGENTS.md`.

DEFINITIONS
- Lease: the right to edit one card, held for a limited time and renewed while in use.
- Edit intent: focus into an editable control, or the first change to a discrete control.
- Arrangement: a card's board and cell, held in a `Placement`.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Scope
The lease shall guard content and relationships. It shall not guard arrangement.

R2 — Acquired on intent
The lease shall be taken on the first edit intent, not on opening the card.

R3 — Leased
The lease shall last 45 to 60 seconds, be renewed about every 15 seconds while the drawer is open and visible, and be taken over on expiry.

R4 — Per session
The lease shall be keyed by user and session. A second tab of the holder shall be told, not locked out.

R5 — Read-only
Where another holds the card, the drawer shall be readable and not editable, and shall name the holder.

R6 — Marked
The card shall show that someone holds it, in a way that cannot be mistaken for an assignee.

R7 — Bulk
A bulk action touching a held card shall refuse as a whole and name the card.

R8 — Arrangement unaffected
A held card shall still be movable between lanes and reorderable.

R9 — Released
Closing the drawer, blur or `pagehide` shall release the lease; the expiry shall cover the rest.

R10 — Rule recorded
The scope rule shall be recorded in `AGENTS.md`.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1, R8: Hold a card in one client; drag it in another; the move lands.
V2 — R5, R6: The second client opens the card; it is read-only and names the holder, and the board marks it.
V3 — R3, R9: Close the holder's tab; the second client can edit within a minute.
V4 — R4: Two tabs of the same person; the second says so rather than blocking.
V5 — R7: Select a held card and another; the bulk action is refused for the whole selection.
V6 — R2: Open a card without focusing a field; no lease is taken.

subtasks.title: Create lock table, conditional endpoints, and record scope rule
subtasks.description: Implement the server-side lock table and conditional lease endpoints, then record the scope rule in AGENTS.md.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `migrations/0004_locks.sql` — one row per held card.
2. `server/workspace/locks.ts` — acquire, renew, release, and who holds what.
3. `POST /api/workspace/items/:id/lock`, `.../heartbeat`, `DELETE .../lock`.
4. `PATCH /api/workspace/items/:id` learns to refuse a non-holder.

DEFINITIONS
- Lease: a lock with a short life, renewed while someone is actually there.
- Holder: the (user, session) the lease names. Two tabs of one person are two sessions.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — One row per card
`item_id` shall be the primary key, so two holders cannot both be right and the race is settled by
the database rather than by a client.

R2 — Conditional, not read-then-write
Acquire shall be one statement that succeeds only when the row is absent or expired. No endpoint
shall read a lock and then write it in a second step.

R3 — The terms the design names
A lease shall live 45–60 seconds. A heartbeat shall extend only the holder's own lease and shall
never create one.

R4 — 423 is not 409
A card held by someone else shall answer **423** with the holder; a stale revision shall stay **409**
with the version. The two are different sentences in the UI and shall stay different on the wire.

R5 — Behind the session
Locks shall be keyed by the server's identity — user and session — and every endpoint shall be behind
the guard task 118.3 added. A holder's name shall be read from the account, never supplied by the
client.

R6 — Content, not arrangement
The write path shall refuse content from a non-holder with 423. Placement writes shall not consult the
lease at all: a card someone is editing can still be dragged.

VERIFICATION
V1 — R1: two sessions acquire one card at once; exactly one gets 200.
V2 — R2: acquire a held, unexpired lease; 423 with the holder, and nothing written.
V3 — R3: a heartbeat extends the lease; a heartbeat after expiry does not resurrect it.
V4 — R4: a held card's content PATCH is 423; a stale-revision PATCH is 409; the bodies differ.
V5 — R6: move a held card; 200, and the move is in its log.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`migrations/0007_locks.sql` — one row per card, `item_id` the primary key, so two holders cannot both
be right. `server/workspace/locks.ts` arbitrates in one conditional upsert (it rewrites the row only
when it has expired, or when it is already this session's), renews only for the holder, releases
idempotently, and answers "who holds this card, if it is not you".

`POST /items/:id/lock` answers 200 or **423** with the holder; `POST .../heartbeat` renews and
answers 409 when the lease has lapsed; `DELETE .../lock` lets go. `PATCH` refuses content from a
non-holder with 423 and never looks at arrangement, which is the content/arrangement split made
real rather than described.

Sessions are tabs: the client sends `x-flowline-tab`, so two tabs of one person are two sessions and
the second is told, not locked out by itself.
subtasks.testStrategy: Exercise acquire/renew/release endpoints directly. Verify two clients cannot acquire the same card concurrently, expiry makes the lock available again, and AGENTS.md contains the recorded scope rule.

subtasks.title: Add presence channel and client lock state
subtasks.description: Establish a workspace presence channel and client-side lock state propagation so holders and other clients see current lease status.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `presence` — a client slice beside the other view state, excluded from `persistedSlice`.
2. The subscription: the workspace channel from task 118.5 carries the lease events.
3. The re-read on connect and on reconnect.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — View state, never persisted
Locks shall not enter `flowline-state-v3`: no persist version is bumped and no migration is written.
A reload starts from the server's answer, not from a remembered lock.

R2 — The events
`lock.acquired`, `lock.renewed` and `lock.released` shall carry the card and the holder, and a release
shall remove the mark at once rather than waiting for a refresh.

R3 — One channel
Presence shall ride the workspace channel task 118.5 opened, not a second connection beside it.

R4 — Reconnect tells the truth
On connect and on reconnect the client shall re-read the held cards, so a socket that dropped during
a handover does not leave a stale name on a card.

R5 — Absence is not freedom
A client that is not connected shall show no lock marks and shall not draw any card as free. What it
may write is the server's answer, not its own guess.

VERIFICATION
V1 — R1: open a card held elsewhere, reload; the mark is there and local storage is unchanged.
V2 — R2: acquire in one client; another names the holder without a reload. Release; the mark goes.
V3 — R4: drop the socket while a lease changes; reconnect; the mark agrees with the server.
V4 — R5: with the channel down, no card is drawn free and the next write is answered, not assumed.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`src/lib/presence.ts` holds the leases this tab can see, and `TAB` names the tab. The leases ride the
same two-second poll as the changes — one request, one cursor, one picture — so a lock and a card
change never arrive from different clocks.

Presence is view state: nothing is persisted, no version is bumped, and a reload starts from the
server's answer rather than a remembered mark.
subtasks.testStrategy: Open two clients in the same workspace. Verify lock events are received by the non-holding client and that client lock state updates without a manual refresh.

subtasks.title: Implement lease acquisition, heartbeat, release, and expiry
subtasks.description: Implement the lease lifecycle on the client: acquire on first edit intent, renew on heartbeat, release on close/blur/pagehide, and allow expiry takeover.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The edit intent in `ItemPanel` — the `startTextEdit`/`endTextEdit` bracket that is already there.
2. The heartbeat, and its pause.
3. Release on close, blur and `pagehide`.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Acquired on intent, not on opening
A card shall be leased when someone begins to edit it, never when they open it to read. Two people
may read one card at the same time.

R2 — Renewed while someone is there
A heartbeat every ~15 seconds shall extend the lease while the drawer is open and the tab visible, and
shall pause when the tab is hidden. Renewal shall stop after a few minutes without an edit, so a
drawer left open overnight does not hold a card.

R3 — Released when they leave
Closing the drawer, blurring the window and `pagehide` shall release best effort. The TTL covers what
those miss; nothing waits for them.

R4 — Taken over on expiry
Another session shall be able to take an expired lease with no steal button, and the person who comes
back shall be told the card moved on rather than have a keystroke dropped in silence.

R5 — Two tabs are one person, told
A second tab of the same account shall be told that the card is open in another tab — not locked out,
and not mistaken for a stranger.

R6 — Coalesced writes outlive the flush
Writes shall be grouped per editing gesture and flushed on blur, close or ~500 ms of idle, and the
lease shall outlive the flush.

VERIFICATION
V1 — R1: open a card; no lease. Focus the title; a lease appears in the other client.
V2 — R2: leave the drawer open past the TTL without editing; the lease lapses. Type again; it is
refused and explained.
V3 — R3: close the drawer; the other client sees it free without waiting for the TTL.
V4 — R4: kill a tab so no release is sent; another client takes the card after the TTL.
V5 — R5: one account in two tabs; the second is told, and neither is locked out.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
`src/lib/lease.ts` takes the pen on **edit intent** — `onFocusCapture` in the drawer, and only for a
field a person could type in, never on opening the card — renews every fifteen seconds while it
holds anything, releases when the drawer closes or moves to another card, and drops everything on
`pagehide`. A renewal that fails drops the lease rather than pretending to hold it.
subtasks.testStrategy: Simulate edit intent, heartbeats, tab blur, pagehide, and expiry. Verify acquisition timing, renewal interval, release behavior, expiry takeover, and same-user second-tab detection.

subtasks.title: Enforce read-only drawer, card mark, bulk refusal, and arrangement exclusion
subtasks.description: Apply UI restrictions for non-holders, mark held cards, refuse bulk actions on held cards, and keep arrangement editable.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `ItemPanel` — read-only for a non-holder, naming the holder.
2. `Card` — a mark distinct from an assignee.
3. The card menu and the bulk bar.
4. Arrangement, which stays untouched.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Readable, not editable
A non-holder shall read every field and edit none. The drawer shall name who holds it, where a person
looks for why they cannot type, and no field shall look editable and then silently refuse.

R2 — A mark, not a badge soup
A held card shall say so on its face, distinguishably from an assignee, a blocker and a priority, and
shall reuse the existing badge shape rather than inventing a second one.

R3 — The card menu agrees with the drawer
A menu item that would change content shall be refused for a non-holder, naming the holder; an item
that only arranges the card shall stay available.

R4 — Bulk refuses as a whole
A bulk content action whose selection includes a held card shall refuse the whole selection and name
the card, rather than applying half of it.

R5 — Arrangement is not gated
Moving and reordering a held card shall be allowed from every surface, because a reader must never
freeze the board.

VERIFICATION
V1 — R1: in a second session, open a held card; every field reads, none edits, the holder is named.
V2 — R2: the card carries the mark, and it is distinguishable from the assignee initials beside it.
V3 — R3: delete from the menu is refused with a name; "move to…" is not.
V4 — R4: select a held card and another; a bulk edit refuses both and names the held one.
V5 — R5: drag a held card between lanes; it moves and the log records it.

PROGRESS — 2026-10-22
R1 is built, and R5 holds by construction: a lease held by another disables every control in the
drawer's body through one `fieldset`, with a banner naming the holder — or saying "open in another
tab" when it is this person's other tab. Nothing is hidden; reading is free, and arrangement is
untouched because a move never goes through the content write path.

Still open: R2 (a mark on the card's face), R3 (the card menu refusing content actions with the
holder's name), R4 (a bulk content action refusing the whole selection), and an e2e where one client
holds a card and another watches it close.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-22
R1 — a lease held by another disables every control in the drawer: the body through one `fieldset`,
the title by hand, because the title lives in the header. A banner names the holder, or says "open in
another tab" when it is this person's other tab. Nothing is hidden; reading is free.

R2 — a held card carries a lock beside its priority, with the holder's name in its title.

R3 — the card menu names the holder and refuses content; "move to" still works, because arrangement
is not the lease's business.

R4 — the bulk bar refuses the whole selection when one of its cards is held, names the holder, and
keeps the two move controls.

R5 — arrangement is untouched: no move path consults a lease, on the client or on the server.

Two faults found on the way, both fixed: the write path was not sending the tab id the lease was
taken with, so a holder was refused their own card; and the lease endpoint required the card to
exist, which would have made a card impossible to edit for the first time — the pen is taken on
intent, before the first write reaches the server.

An e2e has one client take the pen and another read the card closed, then watches it open again when
the holder lets go.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run two-client verification: hold a card in one client and verify the other sees read-only drawer, holder name, distinct card mark, bulk refusal naming the card, and that arrangement moves still succeed.

tasks.title: A refused write keeps the words and says what happened.
tasks.description: This task handles the two refusals a lease produces — someone else holds the card, or it changed while you were typing — without losing text.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The field writes in `src/components/ItemPanel.tsx`.
2. The write adapter's error surface.

DEFINITIONS
- Held (423): another person holds the lease.
- Changed (409): the card moved on under the write.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Distinguishable
A held card and a changed card shall produce different messages.

R2 — Kept
The local text shall stay visible after a refusal.

R3 — Explained
The message shall name the holder, or the change that occurred.

R4 — Offered
The drawer shall offer to copy the local text and to reload the card.

R5 — Stopped
Further writes to that card shall be refused until the person reloads or the lease is released.

R6 — Never replayed
A refused write shall not be retried automatically.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1, R3: Force a 423; the holder is named. Force a 409; the change is named.
V2 — R2, R4: The text remains, and copy and reload both work.
V3 — R5: Keep typing; no further write is sent.
V4 — R6: Wait; no retry is attempted.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Two refusal states, a field that keeps its text, copy and reload, and no automatic retry.

tasks.title: A workspace has members, and a member's role decides what they may do.
tasks.description: This task adds workspaces, invitations, roles and removal.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A workspace entity and the scoping of every persisted entity.
2. Membership and roles.
3. The invitation flow from the auth task.

DEFINITIONS
- Workspace: the container of boards, lanes, items, types, tags and objectives.
- Role: the recorded set of actions a member may take.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Scoped
Every board, lane, item, placement, edge, link, type, tag, objective and log entry shall belong to one workspace.

R2 — Sealed
A person shall see only the workspaces they are a member of.

R3 — Roles
At least owner, editor and viewer shall exist, with a recorded permission table.

R4 — Invitation
An invitation shall be accepted once, by the invited address.

R5 — Removal
Removing a member shall take effect on their next request.

R6 — No escalation
A member shall not grant themselves a higher role.

R7 — Ownership
The last owner shall not be removable while members remain.

RELATED WORKSTREAM
The admin/identity breakdown is tasks 131-149; docs/admin.md is the source. 131-136 and 142 deliver this task's role, invitation, removal and escalation clauses. R1/R2 (workspace scoping) remain task 118's job.

SPLIT — 2026-10-22
This task is an umbrella, so its split is not a second list of the same work. Roles, invitations,
removal and escalation stay with 131-136 and 142; the acceptance pass is 122.3 because nobody else
owns "these add up together". What 118 left undone is the container itself, and that is 122.1 and
122.2.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1, R2: Two workspaces; each member sees only their own, in the UI and the API.
V2 — R3: A viewer attempts an edit; refused.
V3 — R5: Remove a member; their session loses access on the next request.
V4 — R6: Attempt to raise your own role; refused.
V5 — R7: Attempt to remove the last owner; refused.

subtasks.title: The workspace is a row, and every entity names it.
subtasks.description: SYSTEM
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository. Read docs/admin.md section 3.1.

This is the part of task 122 that no other task owns. Roles, invitations and removal are delivered
by 131-136 and 142; what remains here is the container those roles are about — because task 118.1
deliberately stored one workspace per instance and left the boundary to 122.

ORDER
This follows task 132.1: the two axes exist before anything is scoped by them.

SCOPE
1. `migrations/` (the next free number): a `workspaces` row, and a `workspace_id` on every entity
   table that holds work.
2. The read and the writer, carrying the id without the client having to know it.
3. A backfill that puts today's single workspace into one row.

DEFINITIONS
- Workspace: the container of boards, lanes, items, placements, edges, links, people, types, tags,
  objectives, key results, templates, settings and logs.
- The instance's workspace: the one a fresh instance creates, named for the instance.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Every entity belongs to exactly one
Boards, lanes, items, placements, edges, links, people, issue types, objectives, key results, board
templates and the settings row shall each carry `workspace_id`, not null, with a foreign key.

R2 — Backfilled, not guessed
The migration shall create one workspace and assign every existing row to it. It shall not drop
anything, and it shall be safe to run on a database that already has rows.

R3 — The client does not carry it
The workspace shall be chosen by the server from the session, not sent by the browser. No URL, no
header and no body shall be able to point a read at another workspace.

R4 — One, for now
A fresh instance shall create exactly one workspace, named for the instance, and the first person to
sign in shall be its administrator (task 132's first run).

R5 — Both runtimes
The migration shall run through `Database.batch` on D1 and on the Node file driver, and the whole
read shall still round-trip on both.

VERIFICATION
V1 — R1: a fresh database has the column on every table; a board row cannot be written without it.
V2 — R2: a fixture at the old shape, with rows, migrates; every row keeps its id and gains the one
workspace.
V3 — R3: a request that names another workspace is served the session's, or refused; it is never
served the other.
V4 — R5: the round-trip test from 118.1 passes unchanged, and the Node smoke test passes.

subtasks.title: Every read and write is sealed to the workspace.
subtasks.description: SYSTEM
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository. Read docs/admin.md sections 3.1 and 3.3.

SCOPE
1. The server's queries: one scoping helper, used everywhere.
2. The guard: membership is asked per request, never cached on the client's word.
3. The refusal: a workspace you are not in is not an empty workspace.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — One door
Every query that reads or writes work shall be scoped by the workspace the session resolved. The
scope shall be a parameter of one helper, not a clause each author remembers to add.

R2 — Sealed, not filtered
A person who is not a member of a workspace shall be refused — 403 with the reason, or 404 where
naming it would leak its existence — never served an empty board list.

R3 — Asked every request
Membership and role shall be read live on each request, so a removal or a role change takes effect
on the next one without a re-login. No session shall carry a cached role.

R4 — The instance administrator may enter
An instance administrator shall be able to read and administer any workspace without being listed as
one of its members, which is the rule that lets somebody repair a workspace they are not on.

R5 — The write path agrees
`PATCH /api/items/:id` and every later write shall resolve the same scope as the read, so a card id
that belongs elsewhere is a refusal rather than an update.

VERIFICATION
V1 — R1: a search for an unscoped `SELECT`/`UPDATE` in `server/` finds none.
V2 — R2: a signed-in non-member asks for the workspace; 403 or 404, and no rows.
V3 — R3: remove a member mid-session; their next request is refused.
V4 — R4: an instance admin who is not a member reads the workspace and may administer it.
V5 — R5: patch a card id from another workspace; refused, and the row is unchanged.

subtasks.title: The workstream holds together: the acceptance pass.
subtasks.description: SYSTEM
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository. Read docs/admin.md section 7, "Acceptance tests".

The clauses 122 states are delivered by 131-145 across several tasks. This subtask is the one that
proves they add up — because every one of them is a rule about a second person, and a single-person
test cannot see any of them.

SCOPE
1. The acceptance list from the document, as tests.
2. Two people, two roles, one instance, through the real entry points.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — The matrix
Every role × action pair shall be asserted once against `can()`, and every pair that a route enforces
shall be asserted through the route as well. A hidden control is not a permission check.

R2 — The second person
A Viewer shall sign in, read a board, and be refused a write with 403 while no row changes. An
Editor shall write work and be refused board design.

R3 — The lifecycle
An inactive account shall not complete sign-in and shall have no live session afterwards. A role
change shall take effect on the next request. A removal shall end access immediately.

R4 — The safe guards
The last administrator shall not be demotable, deactivatable, deletable or removable; a second
administrator shall make all four possible. A person shall not deactivate or delete themselves.

R5 — The static build is untouched
With no server, the app shall still boot and show what it shows today. None of this may make a board
need an account.

VERIFICATION
V1 — R1: the table is generated from the role list, so a new action without a decision fails.
V2 — R2: two real sessions; the Viewer's `PATCH` is 403 and the stored row is byte-identical.
V3 — R3: deactivate, change a role, remove; each takes effect on the next request.
V4 — R4: the last administrator's four attempts all refuse; with two, all four succeed.
V5 — R5: the e2e suite against the static build passes unchanged.

tasks.expansionPrompt: (1) the workspace entity and the scoping change for every table; (2) membership and the invitation acceptance path; (3) the role table and its enforcement at the API; (4) removal, the last-owner guard and tests.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Workspaces scope every entity already in the schema, which is a schema-wide change, plus roles, invitations, removal and escalation guards.

tasks.title: A board can be shared as a read-only link, and the link can be revoked.
tasks.description: This task adds signed, revocable links that show a board without an account.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A share token bound to a board.
2. The read-only mode of the board view.

DEFINITIONS
- Share token: an unguessable value naming one board.
- Revoked: a token that no longer resolves.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Token
A share link shall carry an unguessable token bound to one board.

R2 — Read-only
The link shall render the board and its cards, and shall offer no editing control.

R3 — No writes
The API shall refuse every write reached with a share token.

R4 — Revoked
Revoking shall stop the link at once.

R5 — Expiry
A link may carry an expiry, after which it shall refuse.

R6 — No account
Opening the link shall not create an account or a session.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R2: Open the link in a private window; the board renders and no editing control appears.
V2 — R3: Attempt a write with the token; refused.
V3 — R4: Revoke; the link no longer resolves.
V4 — R5: Expire a link; refused.
V5 — R6: Check that no user or session was created.
tasks.complexityReasoning: A signed token, a read-only render, an API guard and revocation.

tasks.title: The flows that make the product work are tested end to end.
tasks.description: This task adds a browser suite over the seams that unit tests cannot see — drag and drop, the drawer, board design and import.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. A new end-to-end suite (Playwright), run in the CI workflow.
2. The preview deployment.

DEFINITIONS
- Seam: a place where two store actions are composed by a component, which unit tests do not reach.
- Deterministic: the suite seeds its own workspace and does not depend on the clock.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Drag and drop
A card shall be dragged between lanes and keep the position it was dropped at.

R2 — WIP
On a justify board, cancelling the reason prompt shall leave the card where it was, and answering shall land it where it was dropped.

R3 — Drawer
A test shall edit a title, add a tag, add a person and set a parent.

R4 — Board design
A test shall split a lane, add a cell and remove it, in edit mode.

R5 — Import and export
A test shall export a workspace, import it into a clean state, and compare the boards.

R6 — Deterministic
The suite shall not depend on wall-clock time or on the demo's current contents.

R7 — Gated
The suite shall run on every pull request and fail the workflow.

DELIVERED — 2026-10-21
Seventeen tests over six flows: drag (three), the WIP prompt (two), the drawer (four), board
design (four), the workspace file (two), and the harness itself (two). They run against the built
app, each in a fresh origin, and finish in about ten seconds locally and eighty in CI, where the
browser install dominates.

The job is named `e2e`, waits on `checks`, and publishing waits on it: a red test never reaches
the live app. A failure keeps its traces and screenshots for a week. The ceiling is recorded at
five minutes — generous against eighty seconds, and to be raised deliberately.

R2's evidence is real: putting the WIP drop bug back made both WIP tests fail, and restoring the
line made them pass.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1–R5: The suite passes locally and in CI.
V2 — R2: The cancel case fails when the drop is made to write its position regardless of the seam's answer.
V3 — R7: The workflow runs the suite and blocks on failure.
V4 — R6: Run the suite twice; the results are identical.

subtasks.title: The harness: each test starts from an empty origin, against the built app.
subtasks.description: This subtask adds Playwright, a config, a seeded workspace and one command that builds, serves and runs.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. `e2e/` — a Playwright suite, its config, and a fixture that seeds a workspace.
2. `package.json` — a `test:e2e` script.

DEFINITIONS
- Seeded workspace: the demo the app creates for a fresh origin — deterministic, and free of the wall clock.
- Fresh context: Playwright's per-test browser context, so storage starts empty every time.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Isolated
Each test shall start from an empty origin, so the app seeds its own workspace and no test sees another's edits.

R2 — The shipped build
The suite shall run against the production build (`vite preview`), not the dev server, so what it tests is what ships.

R3 — No clock
No assertion shall depend on the current date. The demo's dates are relative, so tests read titles, positions and counts.

R4 — One command
`npm run test:e2e` shall build, serve and run, and answer non-zero on failure.

R5 — No false green
A failing assertion shall fail the run, and a server that cannot start shall fail it too rather than skipping silently.

subtasks.title: A card dragged between lanes lands where it was dropped.
subtasks.description: This subtask covers the drag: across lanes and within one, asserting the position rather than just the lane.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Between lanes
A card dragged from one lane to another shall appear in the target lane.

R2 — Where it was dropped
The card shall sit at the dropped position: above the card it was dropped above, below the one it was dropped below.

R3 — Within a lane
A card dragged within its own lane shall reorder, and the order shall survive a reload.

R4 — The real gesture
The test shall drive the pointer the way a person does — press, several moves, release — because the app's lift is pointer-driven and a synthetic drag drops the lift.

subtasks.title: The WIP prompt: cancelling leaves the card, answering lands it where it was dropped.
subtasks.description: This subtask covers the justify policy — the case that once failed while every unit test passed.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

DEFINITIONS
- Justify board: a board whose WIP policy asks for a reason before a move that would exceed a lane's limit.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Cancelled
Dropping a card into an over-limit lane shall raise the reason dialog; cancelling shall leave the card exactly where it was.

R2 — Answered
Giving a reason shall land the card in the target lane, at the position it was dropped.

R3 — Recorded
The reason shall be on the card's Activity and on the card itself.

R4 — The regression this exists for
R1 is the case that once failed while every unit test passed: the drop wrote its position regardless of the policy's answer. The test is named after that, so a future refactor of the drop reads it.

subtasks.title: The drawer edits: title, tag, person, parent.
subtasks.description: This subtask covers the four edits the drawer is opened for, and that each reaches the card.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Title
Editing the title shall change the card's title on the board once the drawer closes.

R2 — Tag
Adding a tag from the board's vocabulary shall show that tag on the card.

R3 — Person
Adding a name shall show the person's initials on the card.

R4 — Parent
Setting a parent shall show the lineage on the card.

subtasks.title: Board design: split a lane, add a cell, remove it.
subtasks.description: This subtask covers design mode, and that the controls stay out of the working board.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Split
In edit mode, splitting a lane shall produce the cells it promised.

R2 — Add
A cell added to a container shall accept a card.

R3 — Remove
Removing that cell shall leave the cards it held somewhere valid, by the store's rule — not lost.

R4 — Outside edit mode
The design controls shall not be present on the working board.

subtasks.title: Import and export: a file out, the same workspace back.
subtasks.description: This subtask covers the round trip, and the refusal of a file that is not a workspace.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Export
The Export control shall download a JSON file carrying the workspace's boards and items.

R2 — Round trip
Importing that file into a clean origin shall reproduce the boards and the item count.

R3 — Refusal
Importing a file that is not a workspace shall be refused with a message, and change nothing.

subtasks.title: The suite runs in CI and a failure stops the workflow.
subtasks.description: This subtask wires the suite into the workflow, with a trace left behind when it fails.
subtasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Trigger
The suite shall run on every push to `main` and every pull request.

R2 — Gate
A failing test shall fail the workflow, in a job named `e2e`.

R3 — Evidence
A failure shall leave a trace — screenshot or video — so the run can be read rather than guessed at.

R4 — Ceiling
The suite shall finish inside a recorded ceiling (proposed five minutes). If it does not, the ceiling is wrong and shall be raised deliberately.

tasks.expansionPrompt: (1) harness, seeded state and CI wiring; (2) drag and drop, WIP cancel/resume, drawer edits, board design, import and export; (3) the two-client lease flow once the server exists.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Six flows, one of which needs the server to exist. The risk is flakiness rather than difficulty.

tasks.title: The app is usable with a keyboard and a screen reader.
tasks.description: This task closes the accessibility gaps left by the visual work: focus, announcements, keyboard paths and motion.
tasks.details:
SYSTEM
Flowline, the application in this repository.

SCOPE
1. The drawer and dialogs.
2. The board, its lanes and the drag gesture.
3. The CI workflow.

DEFINITIONS
- Focus trap: focus may not leave an open modal surface until it closes.
- Live region: a polite announcement of a change a sighted user sees.

REQUIREMENTS

R1 — Focus
An open drawer or dialog shall contain focus, and Escape shall return it to the control that opened it.

R2 — Announced
A completed drag, a refused drop and a raised warning shall be announced.

R3 — Keyboard paths
Every action available by drag shall have a keyboard path: move to lane, set parent, reorder.

R4 — Motion
`prefers-reduced-motion` shall be respected.

R5 — Names
Every control shall have an accessible name, and the lane tree shall read as a tree.

R6 — Contrast
The legibility tests shall remain green.

R7 — Automated
An axe check shall run over the key views in CI.
tasks.testStrategy:
VERIFICATION

V1 — R1: Tab through the drawer; focus does not escape, and Escape returns it.
V2 — R2: With a screen reader, complete a drag; it is announced.
V3 — R3: Move a card using only the keyboard.
V4 — R7: The axe job runs and passes.
V5 — R4: With reduced motion enabled, transitions do not run.
tasks.expansionPrompt: (1) focus trap and Escape return in the drawer and dialogs; (2) live-region announcements for a drag, a refusal and a warning; (3) keyboard paths — move to lane, set parent, reorder; (4) axe in CI and reduced motion.
tasks.complexityReasoning: Focus traps and announcements are contained; the hard part is a keyboard path for every drag action, which touches the board's whole interaction model.
